Please note that UNOPS will at no stage of the recruitment process request candidates to make payments of any kind.

Background Information - Sri Lanka

UNOP Sri Lanka Country Office

‍

‍

UNOPS in Sri Lanka is based in Colombo and is responsible for helping the Government of Sri Lanka and partner organizations deliver social and economic rehabilitation in areas affected by the 2004 tsunami and decades of armed conflict. UNOPS in Sri Lanka helps partners achieve their project goals in sectors including physical infrastructure, the environment and poverty mitigation.

UNOPS has supported Sri Lanka’s development since 1998, expanding operations in 2005 to support the post-tsunami response and reconstruction process. Within the organization’s mandate in project management, infrastructure, and procurement, UNOPS Sri Lanka implements customized socio-economic development projects that benefit vulnerable people and develop national capacities. Achievements in Sri Lanka include the development of sustainable and climate-resilient infrastructure, procurement services & capacity building, and project management in education, fisheries, roads, health, water supply systems; flood control and sanitation, and integrated solid waste management sectors. UNOPS works closely with Government counterparts and communities to ensure increased ownership, sustainability, and accountability of Projects.

UNOPS Sri Lanka facilitated over $22 million worth of procurement of COVID-19 protection equipment and services in partnership with the World Bank, the Government of Japan, and the United Nations Multi-Partner Trust Fund. Currently, UNOPS is conducting about $5 million pharmaceutical procurement to strengthen the Sri Lanka health system and support the people in need.

Background Information - Job-specific

Project Information

‍

The Procurement And Technical Support For TVET Career Platform Project In Sri Lanka Will Reduce Unemployment Of Youth, By Creating a Career Platform, With Quality Career Development And Guidance Services. There Are Three Key Outputs That The Project Needs To Deliver

Output 1 : TVET Career Platform is developed and operational

Output 2 : Service Providers’ capacities in TVET Career Platform are strengthened

Output 3 : TVET Career Platform is widely disseminated and utilised among employers and prospect employees.

The project is implemented in the capital of Sri Lanka, Colombo, with a budget of USD 1.1 million and with the funding of KOICA. The Project Manager will be supervising technical personnel, an IT officer and a MEP engineer.

‍

Job- specific information

Project Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the project(s) and provides services to the donor, partners and beneficiaries. Project Manager acts on behalf of the Project Board to manage the project on an ongoing basis during the Implementation Stage. The main responsibility of a Project Manager is to ensure that the project outputs are delivered within the specified project tolerances of time, cost, quality, scope, risk and benefits. He/she is expected to meet the organization’s performance and delivery goals.

Project Manager has the authority to assign, as per the Project Plan, work packages to Team Managers and approve deliverables produced by them.

Project Manager is responsible for creating the Implementation Plan, using the Project Initiation Document (PID), Legal Agreement and having a thorough understanding of the terms, conditions, and the respective roles and responsibilities of the partners/stakeholders, to ensure the project(s) outputs are capable of meeting the business cases for both UNOPS and the partner(s). Success of the project(s) and hence of the Project Manager will be based on the defined Success Criteria.

Functional Responsibilities

Project Delivery and Performance
Develop, complete and update implementation plan(s)
Implement the approved plan (including the establishment of milestones) within tolerances set by the Project Board.
Embed sustainability dimensions including social and gender inclusion, environmental and economic aspects into project life span.
Manage the production of the required outputs, taking responsibility for overall progress and use of resources and initiating corrective action where necessary.
Ensure that quality of work packages and deliverables complies with the quality requirements defined in the Implementation Plan.
Liaise with any external suppliers or account managers
Manage acceptance and delivery of work packages
Monitor project progress ensuring that work packages are being executed properly
Control project and work packages changes
Accept goods, services or works delivered by suppliers.
Lead contract management duties including supplier performance evaluation.
Identify, and anticipate in a timely manner, potential risks and issues and advises mitigating measures to senior management/ Project Board so that maximum benefit to partner(s) and other stakeholders is achieved
Identify and report to the supervisor potential business opportunities for UNOPS
Procedures
Comply with all organizational policy and specifically the Project Management Manual
Prepare/adapt all relevant plans for approval by the Project Board.
Manage the reporting obligations defined in the Legal Agreement(s) and in the Implementation Plan
Draft the requirements definitions for procurement processes. Approving requisitions and requests for non-purchase order payments; Evaluating submissions received, if appointed to the evaluation team.
Ensure maintenance of the project files and lessons learned are recorded
Ensure the development and implementation of project financial management guidelines and control mechanisms, in conformity with UNOPS rules and regulations.
Manage budgets, cash flow and obligations to ensure that deliverables are met and payments to contractors and personnel are received on time.
Understand and manage UNOPS overheads, allocable charges, and related corporate charges as they apply to the project
Understand the unique structures of the UN and budget appropriately for personnel
Manage expenditures against the budget (based on accurate financial reports)
Where the Project Manager has no delegation as a committing officer, s/he retains these responsibilities and will monitor and instruct/request others to carry out the relevant commitments and disbursements.
For project closure purposes, provide a formal handover of the project to the closure manager
Support project audit activities, including planning, preparation and coordination during the audits and follow up on audit observations/recommendations
Monitoring and reporting
Prepare and issue regular project and/or financial reports in accordance with Partner and UNOPS requirements for reporting.
Regularly review project status, evaluating performance criteria (scope, cost, schedule and quality).
Maintain diaries and progress reports as required by the organization’s standard procedures.
Provide routine oversight and analysis of delivery data within the dashboard system.
Ensure all project team members track and regularly update milestones and targets for the duration of projects' life span
Stakeholder engagement
Develop stakeholder profiles and facilitate the formulation of stakeholder engagement strategies
Establish solid working relationships with the Project Board (Executive, Senior Users and Senior Suppliers), client and key stakeholders
Enable the formulation of project communications plans. Coordinate internal project communications. Monitor the effectiveness of project communications
Coordinate stakeholder engagement and communication, ensuring effective timing and interdependency management of communications. Ensure stakeholders are aware of project activities, progress, exceptions and are in a position to accept handover outputs.
Quality assurance
Work with internal stakeholders to ensure projects comply with audit requirements
Work with procurement/purchasing staff to ensure effective interface with suppliers' quality systems
Coordinate quality reviews of project documents and deliverables
Provide quality control for management outputs (project documents, reports, etc.)
Knowledge management and innovation
Encourage routine and effective capacity building activities are conducted in order to build the long-term and sustainable capacity of staff.
Actively interact with other Project Managers and the wider PM community to share case studies, lessons learned and best practices
Contribute to the oversight of lessons learned procedures, ensuring that lessons learnt are shared in a timely and appropriate manner. Participate in the relevant Communities of Practice

jobs.description:
At Bupa,  purpose meets possible
. Join us and help shape a future where healthcare is more connected, more personal and more human.
We’re a global healthcare leader trusted by millions and committed to helping people to live longer, healthier, happier lives and making a better world. Healthcare is changing, and so are we. We’re investing in more clinics, better systems and smarter, more connected ways to help our customers. As we continue to expand our services and invest in innovation, you’ll help create a healthcare system that meets people where they are, responds to what they need and leaves them better than before. Here, your work has purpose, your voice matters and your future is full of possibility.
Just imagine the impact you could make.
Opportunity snapshot -2-year Fixed term contract Opportunity- Business Analyst
Bupa is embarking on a new strategic direction that involves several strategic initiatives, significant changes in
our ways of working and securing our customer data and securing the new Savannah 27 strategy, and to support the delivery of BUPA’s vision of being the trusted preferred partner for healthcare providers.

The purpose of this role is to support the analysis approach and provide analytical services on large complex initiatives, and lead this work on smaller, less complex ones, whilst ensuring processes and requirements for strategic change initiatives are captured, documented and successfully delivered.

The Business Analyst will support the development of new changes over the entire Software Delivery Life Cycle, including in depth analysis of our customer & business needs and pain points; assisting designers, engineers and developers to understand these and how these are represented in our requirements; supporting testing where appropriate and providing project implementation support as required.

Responsibilities 

Partner closely with business initiative owners to develop a deep understanding of the challenges, pain points and areas of opportunity
Assist with scoping and development of work packages
Plan, establish and facilitate stakeholder workshops
Conduct Cost/Benefit Analysis to support discovery and new business investment proposals
Development of current and future state process documentation
Development of business requirement specifications (BRS) and functional requirement specification (FRS) documentation (as required/project specific) and utilising standard templates and guidelines
Challenge and ask 'why' to provide the best solution for the business and our customers
Work closely with cross-functional teams to develop clear and unambiguous product backlogs of work which deliver the outcomes needed by our business
Work with the team to define Epics, Features, User Stories and tasks per business initiative at pace
Define concise acceptance criteria which supports the delivery team and testers
Work closely with the team to refine the backlog and ensure the team has a shared understanding of the content
Proactively support the uplift of Delivery practices and foster a culture of continual improvement, allowing the delivery team to move at pace, yet delivering high quality and secure requirements
Participate in and contribute to the BA and Agile Communities of Practice within Bupa, and to capability uplift and continuous improvement initiatives within the BA practice
Mentor and support Associate Business Analysts and Business Analysts to uplift analysis skills and Domain knowledge as required
Review Test Strategy, review Test Plan, Test Cases and Test Results for SIT, Performance and Security Testing

Requirements 

Experience leading and defining the analysis approach regardless of complexity in projects/Agile product deliveries
Experience collaborating with, supporting and mentoring associate/junior level Business Analysts on the job (desirable)
Experience in establishing and facilitating workshops for Discovery and elicitation or requirements at a senior stakeholder level
Experience with process mapping and applying conventions using MS Visio, Miro and/or Lucid Chart
Delivery experience working within cross-functional teams
Proven experience working with one or more project delivery methodologies - Hybrid, Waterfall and a Scaled Agile Framework
Demonstrated experience working with Agile methodologies and ceremonies including: Backlog Refinement, Daily Standups, Iteration/Release Planning, Showcases/Sprint Reviews
Tertiary qualifications in Information Systems/Information Technology or equivalent (desirable)
High degree of credibility and strong ability to communicate, build trust and forge strong relationships with senior stakeholders and make executive level presentations

Why you’ll love it?

At Bupa, our purpose is to help people live longer, healthier, happier lives and make a better world, and we know this starts with delivering our purpose for our people.   
Our wellbeing program Viva has been designed to help you to live a healthy and happy life. It includes access to health & general insurance discounts, information and education sessions, and preventative healthcare screening such as annual health assessments and skin checks. Through Viva you have access to a range of benefits that will help you to maintain your physical, mental, social, digital, environmental and financial wellbeing. As well as a competitive salary, a range of Bupa benefits and flexible working, you’ll be challenged and encouraged to innovate. 
If this sounds exciting, we’d love to hear from you. Let’s shape the future of healthcare, together.
At Bupa your wellbeing, identity, and personal story are respected and valued. We are continuing to build teams that reflect the diversity of the communities we serve. Bupa is committed to providing equal opportunities and fostering a workplace and environment that is free of discrimination, bullying and harassment.
We actively encourage applicants from all backgrounds and experiences, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, veterans, people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ applicants.
We are dedicated to removing barriers to participation. If you need any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, or if you’d like to discuss how this role can be flexible for you, please let us know so we can support your participation on an equitable basis.

We are seeking a highly motivated Business Program Manager
to lead cross-functional business initiatives that support key organizational priorities. This role requires an experienced program manager who thrives in fast-paced environments, quickly adapts to changing business needs, and consistently delivers high-quality results against aggressive timelines.

The ideal candidate is an organized, proactive professional with strong program management, stakeholder engagement, and analytical skills. They are comfortable navigating ambiguity, driving execution across multiple teams, and leveraging AI and automation to improve operational efficiency and business processes.

Lead cross-functional business programs from planning through execution, ensuring successful delivery of initiatives on time and within scope.

jobs.description:
Join us as an Industrial Project Manager
and lead initiatives that transform how we operate. In this role, you will drive plant-level planning transformation, implement Engineer-to-Order (ETO) standard processes, and lead cross-functional projects that improve operational performance, productivity, quality, and sustainability. You will partner with plant leadership and key stakeholders to execute strategic initiatives, champion continuous improvement, and deliver measurable business results.

What will you do?

Lead the implementation and adoption of ETO standard planning processes across the plant's end-to-end planning activities.
Manage industrial transformation and continuous improvement projects, ensuring delivery on scope, schedule, budget, and business objectives.
Coordinate cross-functional teams and align stakeholders around shared project goals that support plant and organizational priorities.
Coach and support planning teams on standard methodologies, best practices, and process excellence.
Drive the Schneider Performance System (SPS) within the planning function by establishing improvement objectives, monitoring progress, and ensuring sustainable results.
Establish planning standards, governance processes, and key performance metrics to improve consistency and operational effectiveness.
Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including service levels, lead times, forecast accuracy, project milestones, and operational performance.

jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Business Marketing team contributes to our broader mission of ensuring responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence by developing and executing strategies that drive awareness, engagement, and usage for OpenAI’s products and platform amongst core business audiences.

The Strategy & Operations function supports Business Marketing with operating models and cadences; strategic planning; portfolio, resource, and investment management; measurement and organizational learning that empower our teams to move at pace with clarity and confidence.

This is a hybrid role, based in San Francisco Bay Area (preferred) or New York City three days a week.

About The Role

Business Marketing moves quickly, and this role sits close to the work. We’re looking for an analytical, highly collaborative Business Operations Manager who can turn a complex marketing budget into better day-to-day decisions. You will partner with marketing leaders, Strategic Finance, Procurement, Data Science, agencies, and regional teams to plan and pace spend, manage commitments, answer urgent questions, and translate investment data into clear actions. This role is not for someone who prefers back-office operations. You will be embedded in the business, understand what teams are trying to achieve, and help them move faster with confidence.

You will run the operating rhythm for budget administration across a global, highly matrixed team: maintaining a trusted view of allocations, POs, contracts, actuals, forecasts, and risks; reconciling inputs across different marketing functions, regions, and shared services; and surfacing tradeoffs for leadership and Strategic Finance. You will also partner with Data Science to better connect spend to outcomes, lead useful ad hoc analysis, and build AI-enabled tools and workflows that take the friction out of budget management and make the information more timely, intuitive, and genuinely useful.

In This Role, You Will

Own day-to-day budget administration across allocations, forecasts, commitments, purchase requests, purchase orders, invoices, accruals, actuals, and reconciliation.
Partner with Business Marketing leadership and Strategic Finance to operationalize allocation decisions, maintain forecasts, prepare scenarios, and surface tradeoffs.
Work side-by-side with marketing leaders across campaigns, events, agencies, contractors, regions, and shared services to plan, pace, track, and manage spend.
Manage the purchasing and contract lifecycle with Procurement, Finance, Legal, agencies, contractors, and vendors, including POs, SOWs, renewals, rate cards, and commitments.
Maintain a trusted global view of spend; reconcile conflicting inputs, identify variances, duplicate costs, timing differences, and at-risk spend, and escalate material issues early.
Build models, dashboards, and ad hoc analyses that connect investments to business goals and help leaders decide what to fund, reduce, defer, challenge, or escalate.
Partner with Data Science and Analytics to improve how Business Marketing understands ROI, effectiveness, and the relationship between spend and outcomes.

You Might Thrive In This Role, If You

Bring 4+ years of experience in business operations, strategic finance, FP&A, marketing operations, business analytics, consulting, or a related quantitative role in a fast-moving, matrixed organization; B2B business understanding preferred.
Strong hands-on experience with significant, at scale budgets, forecasts, purchase orders, commitments, accruals, invoices, and reconciliation.
Excellent analytical skills and genuine curiosity: you enjoy digging into messy data, answering ad hoc questions, and finding the business story behind the numbers.
Practical understanding of purchasing, contracts, agencies, vendors, and the operational details that keep spend moving responsibly.
Ability to communicate clearly, build trust with marketers and finance partners, and create alignment across different marketing functions, regions, and shared services without formal authority.
An AI-native builder mindset: you see a repetitive spreadsheet, approval, reconciliation, or reporting task and start thinking about how to make it simpler, faster, and more useful.

We are seeking an on-site Sustaining Operations Program Manager (OPM) to oversee our server and rack product lines. jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies, and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

Role

The Implementation Manager owns the deployment of Peregrine's platform across a portfolio of public safety customers. You will direct AI agents through configuration and integration, keep concurrent projects moving, and hold every deployment accountable from kickoff through go-live. In this highly focused role, you will work against a clear metric: timely, successful launches—and we're looking for someone who takes real pride in that.

As An Implementation Manager, You Will

Own the end-to-end deployment lifecycle for a portfolio of customers — from initial kickoff through network connectivity, data source integration, QA, permissions configuration, training, and go-live
Direct AI agents to execute integrations, configure ontologies and data models, and set up customer-specific front-end configurations — translating customer requirements into high-quality agent inputs and rigorously validating outputs
Drive and unblock network access and data source connectivity, including internal coordination with Peregrine's infrastructure and engineering teams and direct engagement with customer IT stakeholders
Facilitate virtual kickoffs and working sessions to align customer stakeholders, establish a project cadence, and map the human terrain of each agency
Run lean, self-service-oriented QA and training sessions that upskill customer POCs to validate their own data and engage Peregrine directly — rather than creating dependency on Peregrine staff
Manage permissions configuration end-to-end: gathering requirements via structured intake, directing agents to translate them into Peregrine, and testing outputs by impersonating roles
Maintain rigorous task management across a concurrent portfolio of deployments, surfacing blockers and escalating with urgency
Identify patterns across your book of business to refine agent prompts, improve deployment playbooks, and raise quality across every future deployment

What Success Looks Like

Deployments you manage achieve significant improvements in speed-to-value, go-live times, and sustained user adoption across the organization
Customer POCs leave your QA and training sessions capable of engaging Peregrine's self-service tools independently, without calling you first
Blockers — whether in networking, credential validation, or customer IT — get surfaced and resolved within hours, not days
Your agent prompts and deployment playbooks improve measurably over time, reducing variance in go-live quality across your portfolio

About You

You are a relentless project manager. You track every open item across your portfolio and hold every stakeholder — internal and external — accountable with precision and care
You are fluent in the language of data systems without necessarily being a data engineer. You know what a credential string is, can tell when a data source isn't connecting, and can work with an engineering team to diagnose and unblock it
You are skilled at navigating complex organizations where individuals may require some AI-upskilling. When there are roadblocks in customer deployments, you stay calm and find the path forward anyway
You are a clear, direct communicator — in writing and in live sessions — and you default to structured, asynchronous information-gathering over unnecessary meetings
You are genuinely curious about AI tooling. You'll be one of the first people at Peregrine to manage a portfolio of deployments primarily through agents, and you'll have strong opinions about how to make that better over time
You are a thoughtful trainer. You know the difference between a customer who is truly self-sufficient and one who just thinks they are — and you close that gap before you sign off

What we look for

3–6 years of experience in enterprise software implementation, technical project management, or customer-facing deployment roles
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent implementation projects against tight timelines
Comfort with technical concepts — data connectivity, credential management, permissions structures, data model configuration — without necessarily writing code
Exceptional written communication and documentation skills; you send clear, structured updates and leave no ambiguity about next steps
Experience working with customers that have limited IT resources or low technical sophistication — public sector or government experience a strong plus
High agency, low ego. You figure things out and you keep moving

Salary Range: $130,000 - $155,000 Annually + Benefits + Equity (if applicable) + Bonus (if applicable)

The Opportunity

Join Adobe as a Program Manager, Transformation, where you will play a pivotal role in driving impactful technology initiatives. This high-utility, flexible role is a great fit for someone who is comfortable with ambiguity and can swiftly adapt to new domains. You will work within a small team of program leaders, contributing to enterprise transformation programs and establishing guidelines that ensure future transformations are repeatable and reliable. Your expertise will be crucial in determining where your skills can yield the greatest benefit to Adobe.

The scope here is broad. You will lead transformation programs end-to-end and, as the portfolio demands, take on specialized responsibilities that span data migration and end-to-end business architecture. You should be equally comfortable ramping on an unfamiliar program and building the reusable standards that make the next program start further ahead.

What You'll Do

Take ownership of transformation programs or workstreams as they arise, ramping quickly and establishing structure, cadence, and momentum.
Partner with FTMO leadership, business users, and technical teams to understand the vision, objectives, and scope of each initiative.
Curate program timelines, roadmaps, and governance — meeting cadence, RAID logs, status reporting, and key artifacts (steering, operating committee, wiki/SharePoint).
Coordinate execution across multi-disciplinary teams; proactively manage risks, issues, dependencies, and changes.
Drive decisions and clear, accurate communication across technical and business audiences.
Flex across the delivery lifecycle — planning, execution, cutover, Hypercare, and decommissioning — depending on where the program needs support.
Measure adoption and impact post-release (30/60/90-day check-ins) and feed insights back into the portfolio.
Adopt and reinforce FTMO best-practice playbooks (migration, cutover, testing, Hypercare, environment/process architecture) on every program, and contribute improvements back to the standard.
On programs that require it, own data migration end-to-end (strategy, plan, ETL cycles, reconciliation, and sign-off) as the single point of accountability, and build the reusable enterprise migration standard that future programs adopt.
When assigned, orchestrate end-to-end business architecture — sequencing environment readiness across the program lifecycle and designing the business process hand-offs across workstreams so the assembled program delivers a coherent end-to-end experience.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; MBA a plus. PMP, PMI-ACP, PgMP, or CSM a plus.
5+ years of program management experience in the software or related technology industry, across a range of program types.

Translate advanced analytics or data science outputs into practical business implications

Act as a bridge between technical analytics teams and business leadership

The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Location:

Posting Details

Posting Details

Posting Number S15662P Working Title Data Analyst II Department PSO-Carl Vinson Inst of Govt About the University of Georgia

Chartered by the state of Georgia in 1785, the University of Georgia is the birthplace of public higher education in America and is the state’s flagship university (https://www.uga.edu/)
. The proof is in our more than 240 years of academic and professional achievements and our continual commitment to higher education. UGA is currently ranked among the top 20 public universities in U.S. News & World Report. The University’s main campus is located in Athens, approximately 65 miles northeast of Atlanta, with extended campuses in Atlanta, Griffin, Gwinnett, and Tifton. UGA employs approximately 3,100 faculty and more than 7,700 full-time staff. The University’s enrollment exceeds 41,000 students including over 31,000 undergraduates and over 10,000 graduate and professional students. Academic programs reside in 19 schools and colleges, including our newly established School of Medicine.

About The College/Unit/Department

The UGA Carl Vinson Institute of Government – Who We Are

As a Public Service and Outreach unit at the University of Georgia, the UGA Institute of Government contributes directly to the university’s overarching public service mission of improving people’s lives by helping to create jobs and prosperity, developing leaders, and addressing critical issues. This public service mission, and the Institute of Government’s role in its success, is at the heart of UGA’s land-grant and sea-grant mission to serve the State of Georgia and its residents.

We have a wide range of experts who inform, inspire, and innovate every day so that governments, large and small, can be more efficient and responsive to their citizens, address current and emerging challenges, and serve the public with excellence. We are uniquely positioned to provide impartial support to local governments and state agencies and convene multi-disciplinary and intragovernmental groups to plan for and address many of the challenges faced by communities across Georgia.

Our areas of expertise and focus include workforce and economic development; infrastructure and community resilience; government operations and organizational effectiveness; measuring and reporting on impact and outcomes; building skills, knowledge and capacity of government leaders and teams; and maximizing technology and data for governments and their leaders.

Whether it is through our award-winning PROPEL (Planning Rural Opportunities for Prosperity and Economic Leadership) program for rural communities, our CyberArch student program that helps Georgia communities increase their cybersecurity, our efforts to build a visionary plan for military and community partnerships to spur economic prosperity and resilient infrastructure, our financial management certificate program to build the capacity of public officials, or hosting educational events about e-mobility strategies for local governments …. We Know Georgia. Fulfilling our land-grant and sea-grant mission to serve the State of Georgia is more than a project. It’s our purpose.

We are growing and excited to add individuals to our team who share our commitment to public service – building stronger communities, inspiring economic resilience, and improving quality of life for communities across Georgia and beyond.

Our Culture – How We Operate

We disseminate knowledge through research, scholarship, and instruction. We collaborate internally across our areas of expertise and across the university with academic researchers to bring best practices and expert insights to the governments and communities we serve. We are committed to fielding a team of experts who have a variety of professional and academic experiences and are grounded in our culture of excellence and approach our work with Georgia’s governments in a comprehensive and objective fashion.

jobs.title: Strategy Analyst - Cross Border
jobs.description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

The Global Cross Border team is responsible for defining the cross border business strategy across travel and eCommerce and managing its execution across our five regions, working closely with market teams and cross-functional leaders around the world.

Cross Border is a key pillar of Visa’s 2030 strategy and one of the largest growth opportunities for Visa. Equally, it faces many complex and interesting challenges, touching all areas of the business, including product, pricing, legal, regulation, marketing, client engagement, and partnerships.

As a Strategy Analyst, you will play an important role in driving the growth and development of our cross border business through travel initiatives focused on issuers, merchants, and end-consumers. Additionally, you will support the buildout of the Visa Destinations platform (destinations.visa.com) by working with the regional and global cross border teams.

The successful candidate will work on innovative strategies that enhance our cross border travel value propositions and effectively target our global customer segments. By leveraging market insights, customer analytics, and competitive intelligence, you will develop and implement strategies across product, loyalty, offers, benefits, marketing services, and key customer segments. This role will interact extensively with regional and functional teams to ensure alignment with the company’s overall goals, driving commercial impact and long-term sustainable growth.

Essential Functions

Build winning strategies across key travel corridors.
Support initiatives to strengthen our XB value proposition and help define our global strategy for target markets and corridors
Help define our global strategy for travel personas (expats, students, etc.).
Support investment prioritization and management across regions.
Support work with key issuers and global clients to increase cross-border PV and market share

Scale Visa Destinations globally, growing our new, differentiated global travel platform.
Help build out and fortify the value propositions of current destinations (e.g. Paris, NY), including sharing best practices
Work with regional XB teams to define the vision, strategy and value propositions of new destinations (e.g. Madrid, Tokyo, Egypt), and support execution.
Support issuer adoption and value creation.

XB Travel Strategy and analytics
Leverage market, competitive and internal data to develop hypotheses and analyses to inform key strategic decisions (e.g. market prioritization, issuer prioritization, etc.)
Support senior management updates and progress tracking

This is a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of strategy, partnerships, and execution
—working with teams and clients around the world. We’re looking for someone who thrives in complexity, thinks globally, and executes with speed.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

2 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD, or PhD)

Preferred Qualifications

3 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or more than 2 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD)
Experience in a strategic, product or international role within a global organization
Understanding of international markets, customer segmentation, and value proposition development, including business case development and go-to-market planning .
Exceptional analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex data and market trends.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with global teams and stakeholders.
Proficiency in project management and the ability to handle multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Experience in consumer financial services and payments is beneficial
Demonstrated success in driving growth initiatives.
Multilingual capabilities are a plus.

Salary may vary depending on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location. jobs.title: Business Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Company Description

Bluebono is building connective infrastructure for the next generation of real estate credit, with a focus on underserved and overlooked market opportunities. Through specialized lending solutions, innovative sourcing, and flexible capital structures, Bluebono connects real estate developers, investors, originators, and institutional capital.
Our platform integrates underwriting, analytics, risk evaluation, servicing, and portfolio management to deliver faster execution, better visibility, and more scalable outcomes across the lending lifecycle.

Role Description

Bluebono is seeking a Business Data Analyst to help build the data foundation and analytical models supporting our lending platform. This role will organize and connect data across the loan lifecycle, develop financial and predictive models, and translate complex information into practical recommendations for management, underwriting, operations, and capital markets.
The ideal candidate combines technical ability with business judgment and is interested in applying data science and machine learning to real-world credit, pricing, risk, and portfolio decisions.

Key ResponsibilitiesData Architecture and Modeling

Design scalable data models covering the loan lifecycle, from initial inquiry and pricing through underwriting, funding, servicing, payoff, or loan sale.
Consolidate data from loan origination, servicing, accounting, CRM, property, pricing, and capital-markets systems.
Build reliable datasets and automated data pipelines for analysis, financial modeling, and machine-learning applications.
Establish consistent data definitions, business rules, validation controls, and documentation across systems.
Identify and resolve missing, duplicated, or inconsistent data in partnership with business teams.

Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics

Develop, test, and refine models supporting lending and operational decisions.
Perform feature engineering using borrower, property, loan, transaction, market, and historical performance data.
Explore applications such as lead conversion, closing probability, pricing, credit risk, loan duration, delinquency, property valuation, fraud detection, investor matching, and liquidity forecasting.
Train, validate, document, and monitor models for accuracy, stability, explainability, bias, and data drift.
Translate model results into clear recommendations while maintaining appropriate human review for material credit and pricing decisions.

Lending and Portfolio Analysis

Analyze loan production, underwriting outcomes, funding activity, servicing performance, payoffs, and loan sales.
Evaluate key metrics including conversion, processing time, LTV, LTC, LTARV, pricing, revenue, funding cost, margin, loan duration, delinquency, concentration, and realized profitability.
Compare projected economics and model predictions with actual results.
Identify trends affecting loan performance, credit quality, operational efficiency, and capital deployment.
Support scenario analysis and stress testing across changes in interest rates, property values, liquidity, and market conditions.

Financial and Capital Markets Modeling

Build loan-level and portfolio-level profitability and cash-flow models.
Analyze funding costs, interest and fee income, servicing revenue, sale proceeds, and transaction expenses.
Model payoff timing, portfolio turnover, liquidity needs, and capital utilization.
Compare performance across products, origination channels, funding sources, and institutional loan purchasers.
Support whole-loan sales, investor reporting, and portfolio-management decisions with accurate loan-level analysis.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Business Analytics, Finance, Economics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field.
At least two years of experience in data analysis, data modeling, machine learning, financial modeling, or a related role.
Strong proficiency in Python, SQL, and Excel.
Experience with data-analysis and machine-learning tools such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
Understanding of regression, classification, clustering, time-series analysis, feature engineering, and model validation.
Ability to work with data from multiple systems and identify gaps, inconsistencies, and unreliable assumptions.
Ability to explain technical findings clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Strong attention to detail, ownership, organization, and business judgment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in mortgage lending, private credit, real estate finance, banking, fintech, or asset management.
Familiarity with bridge, fix-and-flip, construction, or DSCR lending.
Experience building credit-risk, pricing, fraud-detection, property-valuation, prepayment, or cash-flow models.
Experience with APIs, cloud databases, data warehouses, and automated data pipelines.
Understanding of loan origination, servicing, warehouse financing, or whole-loan sales.
Familiarity with model governance, explainability, performance monitoring, and financial-services compliance.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will help Bluebono establish a reliable data foundation, develop models tied to measurable business needs, and turn operational data into better decisions across pricing, underwriting, risk management, capital efficiency, and portfolio performance.

The Research Analyst position marks the entry point for a uniquely powerful career development track – one that can truly lead anywhere. You will also have plenty of freedom to chart your own course, as you grow and develop with our business.

Creativity

– We believe that how you go about business is as important as business results.

Agility

Key Responsibilities

The primary focus of the Research Analyst is supporting the practice in preparing for business development meetings and delivering on executive search projects. Typical job focus includes:

Preparing company overviews for account teams
Researching companies and developing target lists
Identifying potential candidates from a variety of online and proprietary tools
Calling companies to determine organization structure

A successful Research Analyst career path typically includes opportunities for promotion to Associate, which has extensive client contact and business development expectations. Career paths for successful candidates may also include a more senior Research position (e.g. “Knowledge Manager”) for a sector or COE cluster.

Additional Responsibilities For a Research Analyst May Include

Searcher
™
Data Quality Management and Entry:
Consistently inputting and updating highly confidential candidate records in our proprietary Client Resource Management (CRM).

Business Development Support:
Actively participating in designing the search and business development strategy with the Partner and Consultant; pro-active involvement as a valued team contributor throughout the search process from pitch to candidate development.

Candidate ID:
Providing research in support of candidate identification and business development activities of the practice. Develops appropriate candidate “target” lists for Senior Associates using the phone, print materials and a wide range of online information resources.

Internal/External Call Participation:
Attending and/or listening in on kick-off meetings, suggesting possible targets, and attending client briefings/meetings when possible; Attending or listening in on all applicable sector and practice meetings/calls.

Focus on Client and Candidate Service:
Developing a full understanding of the search and the research needs of internal clients; Developing confidence and trust of both internal and external clients.

Market Intelligence:
Teaming up on “proprietary” market intelligence projects in a Research Analyst sector and/or COE industry concentration; Proactively identifying and tracking organizational, industry, and/or functional trends and reporting findings.

YEAR ONE CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS

Learn the researcher role and become an effective member of the search team.

Master ability to identify relevant candidate backgrounds from a variety of sources including:

Searcher Express™ (proprietary candidate database)
LinkedIn, Capital IQ, BoardEx, Pitchbook, ZoomInfo, etc.
Industry associations and trade publications

Manage time effectively to simultaneously balance research requests from multiple search teams. Actively engage with colleagues of all levels to create a culture of transparency, collaboration, respect, execution, and professionalism.

Professional Experience/Qualifications

Intelligence and Intellectual Curiosity:
Must be genuinely interested in learning about people, business and industry characteristics/needs. Need the ability to quickly learn industry fundamentals and understand criteria for success. Importantly, they must have a high "EQ" (Emotional [Maturity] Quotient). Need sufficient conceptual skills to understand broad industry concepts and analytical skills to “drill down” to determine depth of experience.

High Energy Level:
Must work on multiple assignments simultaneously, adhering to best practice guidelines. Must be willing to work hours required to complete the assignment. “ Street Smarts
” The ability to quickly discern the criteria most important for candidate success in a particular search and think in a non-linear fashion so as to work smarter and creatively; Listen to and process candidate information in such a way as to determine likely fit with the opportunity and quickly “close” the conversation to specific next steps or additional source or candidate identification.

Contribution to Resources:
Adds to and updates Searcher. Conducts a thorough evaluation of the outcome of research provided on a search and ensures that results are recorded in Searcher. Actively contributes to the practice knowledge system as well as to practice and research meetings.

Entrepreneurial Spirit:
Works with minimal direction; is a self-starter but at the same time knows when to, and is comfortable with asking for direction when necessary. Provides meaningful feedback and when appropriate offers value-added suggestions for approaching the search in a different way. Provides research support in business development efforts.

Efficiency and Need for Closure:
Work with multiple managers and prioritize task effectively. The ability to understand to complete searches quickly and at the highest quality standards, while making a profit consistent with the value delivered.

Persistence and Thoroughness:
Ability to work in a fast-paced and unstructured work environment, able to assertively navigate organizational structures, but with sensitivity and finesse. Associates must reliably complete necessary paperwork and follow procedures effectively, especially those involving protecting key assets, such as proprietary databases.

Outstanding Communication Skills:
Although outstanding telephone skills are especially essential, Associates need excellent overall communications skills, as well. They must demonstrate excellent verbal skills on the telephone, written skills in drafting specifications and references as well as other required documents, and presentation skills in client situations.

Discretion:
Must project an understanding and appreciation for the strict confidentiality of client and candidate information and protect it as appropriate.

Poise and Professional Presence:
Although in-person client contact is not the primary focus of this position, the Research Analyst will interface frequently with very senior stakeholders, and must project a professional image.

Positive Cultural Influence:
Although our culture is independent and entrepreneurial, a team orientation is becoming increasingly important. At a minimum, the Associate must interface well with other office associates, but ideally will become a valued and important part of building a positive culture, raising other associates' job satisfaction levels, and increasing office productivity and retention rates.

LEADERSHIP CHARACTERISTICS

Getting Organized:
Is well-organized, resourceful, and focused; effective and efficient at marshalling multiple resources to get things done; lays out tasks in sufficient detail to mark the trail; gets things done with less and in less time; can work on multiple tasks at once without losing track of any; foresees obstacles and plans around them.

Focusing on Action and Outcomes:
Attacks everything with drive and energy with an eye on the bottom line; unafraid to initiate action before all the facts are known; drives to finish everything he/she starts.

Communicating Effectively:
Writes and presents effectively; adjusts to fit the audience and the message; gets a message across with precision, clarity, brevity, and a relentless desire to re-read / proofread.

Managing Up:
Is ambitious and is comfortable marketing himself/herself to higher management; knows how to relate effectively to top management, and can advocate for him/herself

Relating Skills:
Warm, friendly, and interpersonally agile; easy to approach and talk to; relates well to all kinds of people; makes a pleasant first impression and builds solid relationships.

Managing Diverse Relationships:
Relates well to a wide variety of diverse styles, types, and classes; open to differences; effective up, down, sideways, inside, and outside; builds diverse networks; quick to find common ground; treats differences fairly and equitably; treats everyone as a preferred customer.

Demonstrating Personal Flexibility:
Open to lifelong, continuous personal improvement; aware of self and impact on others; responsive to feedback; is very flexible; can act in ways that seem contradictory and is adaptable to demand characteristics of different situations.

EDUCATION

An undergraduate degree from a well-regarded institution is required. Familiarity with Microsoft Office Products and databases (such as Bloomberg, Factiva, Lexis-Nexis) are a plus.

jobs.title: Research Analyst - Evidence Aggregation and Data Science at Northwestern University
jobs.description:
Research Analyst – Evidence Aggregation and Data Science

Global Poverty Research Lab, Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University

What does the Lab do?

The Global Poverty Research Lab (GPRL) is a research center based at Northwestern University that accelerates poverty reduction by generating frontier research and creating public goods in the form of data, methods, and syntheses, to enable others to design, test, and turn evidence into action.

Projects At GPRL Cut Across The Following Pillars

Frontier Research: Generate cutting edge research in development economics including themes of mental health, agriculture, social protection, and renewable energy; co-create and maintain long-run panels with local universities, governments, and civil society that enable longer-term insights and support layered RCTs.
Advance Research Methods: Build and test better ways to measure and learn, from questionnaire design and enumerator recruitment to rapid-cycle experiments (A/B, factorial, micro-randomized) that implementers can run using their own administrative data to tune delivery models, incentives, and other protocols.
Aggregate Global Evidence: Building semi-automated pipelines and AI-assisted workflows to compile and structure scattered evidence from RCTs into living knowledge bases and run rigorous meta-analyses; deliver insights via evidence syntheses, interactive dashboards, and publicly accessible data for donors, investors, and practitioners.
Making Aid More Effective: Turn evidence into ready-to-use decision tools, “smart buys” menus, and ROI/cost-effectiveness frameworks for donors, ministries, multilaterals, impact investors, and social enterprises.

Our Team

GPRL is co-directed by Dean Karlan, Christopher Udry, and Nancy Qian, professors at the Kellogg School of Management and the Weinberg School of Arts and Sciences’ Economics department at Northwestern University. Other actively affiliated professors include Andrew Dillon and Lori Beaman. GPRL’s research managers, research analysts, and administrative staff support our investigators’ projects, in the process working closely with colleagues at universities, NGOs, and research institutions around the world.

GPRL also works in close collaboration with research teams at Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) to coordinate field data collection, disseminate evidence, and create shared training and research resources.

Job Summary

GPRL is hiring 2 full-time Research Analyst – Evidence Aggregation and Data Science to support our Evidence Aggregation Initiative, a multi-institution effort to build scalable, AI-assisted infrastructure for compiling and synthesizing evidence from randomized controlled trials in development economics. The initiative spans the full pipeline from study selection and AI-assisted data extraction to microdata harmonization, meta-analysis, and public dissemination — with the goal of making the best available evidence on what works for whom more accessible to researchers, policymakers, and donors worldwide.

This position offers a rare opportunity to work at the intersection of data science, AI, and development economics research. The RA will contribute to a live, rapidly evolving pipeline at a moment when the project is scaling up from a pilot phase to broader operations. They will gain hands-on experience building and maintaining research data infrastructure, working with large language models in applied research contexts, conducting quantitative analysis, and supporting the management of a distributed network of data validators. The role suits candidates with strong technical skills who are equally motivated by the real-world impact of the work.

Core Responsibilities

Supporting the operation and iterative improvement of the AI-assisted data extraction pipeline, including monitoring extraction accuracy, identifying fields where AI performance requires refinement, and contributing to validation workflows
Cleaning, organizing, and quality-checking data extracted from several published RCT papers into DEVIDENCE, GPRL's relational database of study-level metadata and treatment effects, and preparing it for use in cross-study analyses.
Cleaning and organizing study microdata from published RCTs and validating their replication packages to prepare them for harmonization and cross-study analyses.
Supporting the crowdsourcing platform through which a distributed network of external validators review and adjudicate AI-extracted data, including helping to onboard new cohorts of validators, tracking coder performance, and identifying and resolving data quality issues
Conducting quantitative analysis using the harmonized data, including contributing to meta-analyses and evidence reviews, preparing tables and figures, and assisting with revisions to working papers and publications
Supervising undergraduate RAs engaged in data extraction and validation tasks, including providing training, reviewing work, and maintaining coding documentation
Contributing to the development and refinement of training materials, coding guides, and documentation that support both internal staff and the external validator community
Assisting with the design and implementation of data harmonization protocols for select outcome variables across studies, including writing and reviewing code that standardizes variables for cross-study comparability
Supporting project management and dissemination tasks, including tracking project milestones, preparing materials for funder and partner communications, and contributing to grant proposals and reports
Conducting literature reviews in support of meta-analyses, evidence syntheses, and grant proposals
Supporting research staff with Lab-wide management tasks including mentoring new RAs, creating research and training resources, and supporting with recruitment

Minimum Competencies

Strong programming skills in R, combined with a willingness to learn other statistical software. Strong quantitative skills, including coursework in statistics, econometrics, or a related quantitative field
Familiarity with randomized controlled trials
Excellent organizational skills
Fluency and excellent communication skills in English
Ability to seek resources and self-teach new statistical, analytical, and programming techniques
Flexible, self-motivating, able to manage multiple tasks efficiently, and work in teams

Preferred Competencies

Familiarity with relational databases and structured data (e.g., SQL or equivalent experience working with multi-table datasets)
Experience living or working in a developing country
Experience with reproducible research workflows, version control (GitHub), and modern documentation tools (Quarto, R Markdown)
Familiarity with meta-analytic methods or systematic review approaches
Demonstrated ability to build data quality assurance systems and manage collaborative data projects
Experience using advanced data infrastructure such as relational databases, API connections, and cloud computing
Familiarity with Stata and/or Python preferred
Familiarity working with a variety of machine learning models
Familiarity with other statistical, visualization or digital data collection software like ArcGIS/Python/SurveyCTO is a strong plus

The research analyst will work in an open, collaborative environment with other GPRL staff in our common lab space at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois (bordering Chicago). The position offers the opportunity to interact with undergraduates, graduate students, and faculty from Kellogg and the department of economics at Northwestern, as well as research staff at IPA. It is well-suited for candidates interested in pursuing graduate study in economics or other social sciences in the future. It is also a great steppingstone for those wanting to explore non-academic careers in the field of development economics. The research analyst will be a full-time employee of Northwestern University with full benefits (including the ability to take classes at a highly subsidized tuition rate).

We are looking for a minimum commitment of two years for this position.

The Research Analyst will support the evaluation of the Economic Liberation Project by coordinating data collection, conducting quantitative and qualitative analysis, producing reports and presentations, and collaborating with community partners and the evaluation team to disseminate findings. The Institute for Research on Labor and Employment (IRLE) is a multidisciplinary research center dedicated to advancing labor research and education for workplace justice.

Position Summary

The Research Analyst will support the evaluation of the Economic Liberation Project for the POWER team. Key responsibilities include coordinating research and evaluation data-collection efforts; cleaning, coding, and analyzing data; writing reports and briefs; and disseminating findings. The role requires active engagement with community partners and stakeholders in Long Beach, California. The Research Analyst will collaborate with the evaluation team to produce reports and create visually compelling materials for diverse audiences.

About The Opportunity

Job Summary

Under the supervision of the Data Quality & Research Administration Analytics Manager and with support of senior level team members, the Senior Data Analyst will work closely with key stakeholders to identify and conduct data analysis projects that support the mission and goals of the University and Northeastern University Research Enterprise Services (NU-RES). The Senior Data Analyst will provide support to key projects through data collection, computational support, and data interpretation and reporting, and will ensure data accuracy and consistent reporting by designing and creating optimal processes and procedures to systematize the data reporting process. The incumbent will use advanced data modeling, predictive modeling, and analytical techniques to develop reports used in key data submissions to internal and external stakeholders. Possess a good sense of humor, ability to be calm under pressure, and effectively communicate with report requestors to ascertain requirements for reports that tell an accurate story.

This job may also be based in Boston. If you are based in the United States, please apply here

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in a relevant subject area (e.g., computer science, data science, mathematics, statistics, information technology, or related field); 3+ years of experience with querying databases, SQL, and Microsoft Excel; experience developing robust dashboards using Tableau and/or Power BI; creating visuals using data visualization best practices.
Proficiency with business intelligence and reporting tools such as Cognos or Snowflake preferred.
Understanding of, and experience in, using analytical concepts and tools, including data modeling and predictive analytics.
Project management, time management, and communication skills necessary to execute responsibilities in a collaborative, academic setting.
Teamwork and collaboration in a professional setting.
Demonstrated curiosity, problem-solving skills, and ability to meet deadlines.
Excellent written and oral communication skills with ability to advise and clearly communicate ideas and results to non-technical audiences.
Strong ability to manage multiple assignments while working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
Ability to maintain a positive attitude and work well independently, within a team environment, and with external users as well as a variety of internal audiences.
Experience working with university research administration data and systems preferred.
Experience documenting business procedures and processes preferred.
Understanding of, and experience in, using AI-enabled tools to provide appropriate levels of support to daily work.
Familiarity with electronic research administration (eRA) systems (e.g., Coeus, ePAWS, or similar eRA platforms) preferred.

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities

45% — Data Collection, Assessment, Interpretation, and Reporting

Collect relevant data (both internal and external) to be used by college constituents to support decision making and strategic direction, resource allocation, internal and external reporting, and other operational decisions. Success factors include the accuracy and relevance of the data, analysis, and the clarity and usefulness of final reports. Develop and iterate on self-service reports and dashboards with an eye towards automation and re-use. Manage data sourced from both legacy systems (e.g., Coeus) and current eRA platforms (e.g., ePAWS 2.0), ensuring continuity and accuracy across reporting environments.

25% — Data Visualization

Oversee the development and maintenance of key performance dashboards that show progress toward strategic and operational goals related to research. Work closely with Research Enterprise Services stakeholders to identify opportunities for additional dashboard requirements as needs evolve. Develop and iterate on self-service reports and dashboards with an eye towards automation and re-use. Tools include Tableau (including Tableau Prep and Tableau Server), Cognos, and other visualization platforms as applicable.

10% — System Support

Evaluate and test back-end changes to electronic research administration systems as they impact data quality and access, including connectivity with Tableau and the Cognos Data Warehouse environment. Monitor data quality in reports and adjust as needed. Support migration activities between legacy and current systems, including data validation and reconciliation tasks.

10% — Process Improvement

Identify opportunities to define areas for process improvement and work with stakeholders to design and build technical processes that improve efficiencies and address business issues and needs. Develop and maintain documentation of data pipelines, reporting logic, and source-of-truth definitions to support team continuity and institutional knowledge.

10% — Ad Hoc Duties

Perform ad hoc research and analysis to support special projects and strategic initiatives serving faculty and staff across Research Enterprise Services in meeting their reporting and analytical needs. May include supporting AI-assisted data extraction, research analytics benchmarking, and cross-institutional data collaborations.

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority is North America's largest transportation network, serving a population of 15.3 million people across a 5,000-square-mile travel area surrounding New York City, Long Island, southeastern New York State, and Connecticut. The MTA network comprises the nation’s largest bus fleet and more subway and commuter rail cars than all other U.S. transit systems combined. MTA strives to provide a safe and reliable commute, excellent customer service, and rewarding opportunities.

Job Summary

The Performance and Strategy Analyst Level I supports the Office of Consolidated Pensions by driving operational excellence, elevating performance measurement, and advancing strategic modernization initiatives across pension operations.

This role builds the analytical foundation for performance management by developing key performance indicators (KPIs) and objectives and key results (OKRs), creating data-driven tools such as Power BI dashboards, and supporting process improvement efforts. This level focuses on strengthening day‑to‑day operational insight, enabling efficient decision-making, and enhancing the member experience through accurate, timely, and measurable service delivery.

Across both levels, the Performance and Strategy Analyst exists to provide the analytical, performance‑management, and strategic support required for a modern, high-performing pension function. Examples of duties include designing new analytical frameworks—such as a suite of Power BI dashboards covering monthly pension inceptions, benefit calculations, retroactive payments, death benefits, Tier 6 member data, and disability retirement processing—and ensuring these tools draw directly from PeopleSoft where possible. The role also contributes to defining and tracking KPIs and/or OKRs to benchmark and continually improve pension operations.

Responsibilities

Develops and maintains performance measurement frameworks (Key Performance Indicators and Objectives and Key Results) to monitor operational efficiency and strategic progress, ensuring leadership has actionable insights for decision-making.

Coordinates and tracks strategic technology enhancements, including targeted PeopleSoft improvements such as end-to-end workflow for pension inceptions, to expand automation and improve the member experience.
Designs and produces monthly and quarterly performance dashboards and reports to provide transparency on operational outcomes and progress toward strategic objectives.
Supports organizational decision-making by developing and managing a lightweight, repeatable decision framework that accelerates approvals and ensures decisions are data‑driven and documented for accountability
Conducts process mapping and analysis to identify bottlenecks and recommend improvements that reduce cycle times, enhance accuracy, and strengthen compliance.
Prepares benchmarking readiness materials, including cost‑per‑member and service‑level metrics, to position the organization for participation in CEM global pension benchmarking and other industry best‑practice comparisons.
Facilitates and supports team workshops focused on agile practices, trust‑building, and integration planning to foster a culture of continuous improvement and collaboration.
Performs other duties as assigned
Complies with all policies and standards

Required Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Knowledge of data analysis concepts, performance measurement practices, and basic process‑improvement methodologies, with the ability to apply these skills to public pension operations.
Working knowledge of pension plan member data or other public‑sector benefits data, including understanding data structures, data quality considerations, and operational workflows.
Skill in analyzing operational data related to public pension administration, such as benefit processing timelines, member transactions, and service‑delivery metrics.
Proficiency with Power BI, including the ability to build dashboards, create visualizations, and connect to enterprise data sources such as PeopleSoft.

jobs.title: Senior AI Program Manager
jobs.description:
Company Description

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Why join Harvard Medical School?

Harvard Medical School's mission is to nurture a diverse, inclusive community dedicated to alleviating suffering and improving health and well-being for all through excellence in teaching and learning, discovery and scholarship, and service and leadership.

You’ll be at the heart of biomedical discovery, education, and innovation, working alongside world-renowned faculty and a community dedicated to improving human health. This is more than a job - it’s an opportunity to shape the future of medicine.

Job Description

Prof. Marinka Zitnik invites applications for the position of Senior AI Program Manager at Harvard University. This role provides a unique opportunity to participate in cutting-edge research at the intersection of AI, medicine, and biology while fostering collaboration within a world-class academic environment.

We are seeking a creative, ambitious, highly motivated, experienced individual to join our lab of graduate students and postdoctoral fellows. The Senior AI Program Manager is responsible for the operational side of the lab's national and international research initiatives, working closely with Prof. Zitnik to support the translation of cutting-edge AI research into biomedical discovery. This position requires a combination of technical background, strong organizational skills, and the ability to communicate effectively across academic and scientific domains.

Key responsibilities include:

Create sponsor reports, progress updates, technical documentation, tutorials, and outreach material, and maintain public-facing project documentation.
Lead operational contact for lab collaborations, industry and frontier AI lab partners, and foundation sponsors, contributing to partner meetings and tracking commitments and follow-up actions on behalf of the PI.
Overseeing and tracking multi-site research projects, including project milestones, deliverables, and dependencies across collaborating sites, data onboarding, and resolving scheduling and resource conflicts.
Managing activities related to reporting deadlines, data use agreements, material transfer agreements, and institutional review submissions.
Overseeing onboarding of new students onto lab resources, planning and executing workshops, seminars, and site visits, handling recruitment logistics, and managing computing accounts supporting the research program.
Responsible for lab meeting operations including confirming schedules and rotation of presenters, overseeing recurring project and collaborator calls across time zones, and creating and circulating agendas and notes.
Maintaining records of software releases, datasets, and project websites, verifying that documentation, licenses, and links remain current, and partnering with project leads on release timing and public announcements.

As part of your application, we recommend including a cover letter, curriculum vitae, 2-3 representative publications or examples of written technical documentation, 2-3 examples of written research proposals or research reports
, that will help us better understand your qualifications and background. This can provide valuable insight into your experience and interest in the role.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Minimum of five years’ post-secondary education or relevant work experience.

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

M.S, Ph.D. or equivalent degree in computer science, engineering, computational biomedicine, technology and operations, or a related field is strongly preferred.
A strong technical background in AI or computational sciences, with familiarity in biology or medicine.
Exceptional writing skills, with experience producing high-quality technical content such as research papers.
Strong verbal communication skills, capable of presenting complex ideas clearly to academics and non-specialists.
A proven ability to represent academic research projects in meetings with collaborators, institutions, and foundations.
Experience with academic partnerships, including writing research proposals.
Excellent organizational abilities, with experience in managing projects, timelines, and resources.
Previous experience in an academic research setting is strongly preferred.

Additional Information

Term: This is a one-year term position from the date of hire, with the possibility of extension, contingent upon work performance and continued funding to support the position.
Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week
Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position.
Pre-Employment Screening: Identity
Staying Informed About Your Application: Due to the high volume of applications, we may not always be able to reach out right away, but you can track your status anytime through the Careers@Harvard portal.

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that all duties and responsibilities must be performed at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location. Certain visa types may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment.

Salary Grade and Ranges

This position is salary grade level 057. Please visit  Harvard's Salary Ranges  to view the corresponding salary range and related information.

Benefits

Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generous paid time off including parental leave
Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one
Retirement plans with university contributions
Wellbeing and mental health resources
Support for families and caregivers
Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement
Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks

Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page.

Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard's academic purposes.
