Job Description

This role will sit in our Nashville, TN office.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is looking for an experienced Lead Technical Program Manager to drive the technical program strategy across our programs. This will include managing key stakeholder relationships with our internal engineering service teams to establish the program requirements, success criteria, and key deliverables.

This is a senior individual contributor role, you will face a broad range of requirements posed by internal and external sources with the challenge of determining the appropriate path forward. It will also require understanding the technical dependencies of a service while applying an aptitude for the customer experience.

A successful candidate will have a passion for technical program management and has strong experience leading a dispersed working group to achieve shared business objectives. Professional experience in large enterprise technology is valued.

Partners with senior management and stakeholders to align priorities and goals using technical know-how in a fundamental engineering area or technical domain. Establishes scope and milestones for each aspect of a technical program, aligning to the broader program plan and company strategies and goals, managing efforts between cross-functional teams to deliver programs or services. Shapes and leads technical programs and highly complex, cross-organizational initiatives impacting products and business. Drives the management of and responses to issues, bottlenecks, and risks, serving as a point of escalation for all issues. Shapes program improvement strategies, leveraging best practices to drive transformational change and optimize processes across multiple teams. Shapes technical program improvement strategies, leveraging best practices to drive transformational change and optimize processes across multiple teams. Shapes technical collaboration across multiple teams, ensuring alignment of priorities and program goals. Provides expert technical guidance to shape and direct the automation of comprehensive reporting, leading collaboration with development teams to drive innovations in reports, dashboards, forecasts, and models for long-term technical program execution. Shapes the strategic direction of collaboration efforts as a technical liaison across stakeholder teams for high-impact technical programs.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Technical Management and Execution - Technical Management:

– Leverages technical knowledge to identify risks, manage scope, estimate program timelines, request feasibility, testing requirements, and determine appropriate resources.

– Designs and shapes the strategy for product or service delivery, ensuring alignment with the third party, security, export, and accessibility compliance requirements.

– Integrates program demands and resourcing.

– Leads rapid response to the most critical security escalations, coordinating across teams and departments and serving as the primary point of contact to executives to assess risk, determine comprehensive mitigation strategies, and ensure alignment and execution of the most effective path to resolution.

– Leads the transformation and optimization of processes to ensure the highest reliability and resilience of products or services.

Technical Management and Execution - Technical Strategy and Execution:

– Utilizes technical knowledge to identify and manage program dependencies and risks.

– Supports rapid response to escalations, coordinating within team and communicating to senior team members to assess risk, determine mitigation strategies, and execute the optimal proposed path to resolution.

– Shapes overall planning activities, ensuring alignment with enterprise architecture.

– Defines and enforces delivery standards and guidelines, ensuring security, scalability, and alignment with best practices.

– Develops Line of Business (LOB) strategies for change management and/or incident response to enhance operational efficiency.

Program Oversight - Strategy and Decision-Making:

– Leads the alignment of priorities with customers, service, and stakeholder teams through regular reporting to stakeholders and senior leadership.

– Establishes scope and milestones, aligning to the broader program plan and company strategies and goals, managing efforts between cross-functional teams to deliver programs or services.

– Leads efforts to define and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and measurement methods for LOB performance.

– Develops and communicates a comprehensive and strategic communication strategy of highly complex objectives to partners and customers.

Program Oversight - Program and Operations Management:

– Shapes and leads both technical and non-technical programs and highly complex, cross-organizational programs impacting products and business.

– Guides and mentors program staff (e.g., development, release management, customer success), providing expert technical support and strategic direction on removing barriers, including risks and issues in workflows.

– Provides guidance on developing and maintaining comprehensive program documentation (e.g., status reports, program plans) and develops risk mitigation strategies.

– Ensures attention to detail, including security and quality, in program management, from planning to execution and reporting.

– Chairs regular program status meetings, fostering collaboration and driving effective communication across teams and leaders.

– Partners with leadership to set service level agreements (SLAs) and productivity benchmarks aligned with long-term business goals.

– Shapes and leads forecasting program demands, funding, and resourcing.

– Leads the deployment of change management for programs, such as priority, scope, scheduling, development, requirement changes, and support.

Program Oversight - Risk Management:

– Drives the management of and responses to issues, bottlenecks, and risks, serving as a point of escalation for all issues.

– Develops plans based on the results of cost assessments, benefits analysis, and return on investment (ROI) to improve decision-making and risk mitigation strategies.

– Makes strategic decisions, balancing business needs, technical constraints, and long-term goals.

– Removes critical blockers for the program and determines optimal technical and resource options to drive the successful delivery and adoption of solutions.

Process Efficiency - Process Optimization:

– Shapes program improvement strategies, leveraging best practices to drive transformational change and optimize processes across the LOB.

– Leads the development and optimization of program objectives and workflows, while orchestrating the deployment of cross-functional solutions to address complex business problems.

– Collaborates with management to innovate and optimize processes and procedures to drive achievement of LOB goals.

Process Efficiency - Continuous Improvement:

– Champions LOB-wide integration of continuous improvement within programs, ensuring alignment of insights across many workstreams with business objectives and operational efficiency goals.

– Establishes and champions best practices for leveraging data insights at scale, influencing senior leadership decisions.

– Leads the development of innovative business-critical improvements to the solution's availability and reliability.

– Iterates processes based on feedback and KPIs, analyzing results through retrospectives.

– Defines requirements and configurations of existing and new development tools, where applicable.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Cross Functional Collaboration:

– Shapes collaboration across multiple teams, ensuring alignment of priorities and program goals.

– Leads process improvements across the LOB, working with senior leaders to implement team-wide efficiency-driven solutions.

– Communicates strategic program updates and insights to leadership teams, shaping decisions at the LOB level.

– Develops and refines engagement approaches for key stakeholders, ensuring informed decision-making at scale to improve program planning and execution.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Program Leadership:

– Shapes and leads programs to optimize organizational efficiency.

– Provides visionary technical direction and mentorship to cross-functional teams.

– Drives transformative change at all levels of the LOB, from initiation through delivery, while ensuring alignment with strategic goals.

– Ensures that the program team and other stakeholders are aligned with the program goals and motivated, identifying and addressing conflicts and issues.

Data and Analysis:

– Shapes and directs the automation of comprehensive reporting, collaborating with development teams to drive continuous improvement of reports, dashboards, forecasts, and models for program execution.

– Utilizes data insights to solve highly complex problems impacting the success of the program(s), including adherence to SLAs.

– Conducts analysis on a large number of data sources with high complexity, which may include competitive analysis, trend analysis, and KPI analysis, to drive data-informed decisions to support the program goals, presenting findings with immediate teams stakeholders.

Stakeholder Engagement:

– Shapes the strategic direction of collaboration efforts across stakeholder teams for high-impact programs.

– Serves as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders, ensuring alignment between program priorities and business objectives.

Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is seeking a Lead Principal Program Manager to lead critical capacity and demand planning programs supporting OCI’s AI/ML and cloud infrastructure priorities. This role will translate business strategy, customer demand, product roadmaps, and deployment readiness into integrated near-term and long-range capacity plans across GPU, compute, storage, and network infrastructure.

Operating at the intersection of Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Data Center Delivery, Capacity Management, Supply Chain Operations, and Finance, this leader will bring clarity to highly ambiguous planning challenges where supply availability, site readiness, capital commitments, deployment timing, revenue realization, and customer priorities must be balanced.

The successful candidate will serve as a trusted partner to senior leaders, lead complex cross-organizational initiatives with a high degree of autonomy and accountability, and establish the governance, analytical frameworks, and operating rhythms required to scale OCI effectively. The role will translate complex business and technical inputs into executive-level recommendations that drive measurable business outcomes, improve decision quality, and optimize capital efficiency and margin performance.

Responsibilities

Own the strategy, planning, and execution of major OCI capacity and demand planning programs affecting core infrastructure products and global deployment operations.
Develop and govern integrated consensus demand plans across customers, initiatives, regions, sites, products, SKUs, and planning horizons, including baseline, upside, and risk-adjusted scenarios.
Translate demand forecasts into executable supply, manufacturing, allocation, and deployment plans by identifying constraints, dependencies, decision points, and required resource commitments.
Integrate New Product Introduction (NPI) roadmaps and product lifecycle transitions with demand, qualification, supply, manufacturing, and deployment plans to enable scalable platform ramps while minimizing capacity gaps and stranded inventory.
Establish and scale cross-functional operating cadences, governance models, KPI frameworks, and executive review mechanisms that improve visibility, accountability, alignment, and decision-making.
Lead high-value capacity and capital decisions involving long-lead components, supplier commitment windows, site readiness, allocation alternatives, cost of capital, inventory exposure, customer delivery, and revenue timing.
Develop clear decision frameworks and recommendations using scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, financial modeling, break-even analysis, and expected-value assessment.
Evaluate end-to-end supply chain and deployment constraints across CPU, GPU, networking, storage, racks, power, space, and data center dependencies; drive mitigation, reallocation, prioritization, or re-baselining before critical deadlines.
Define performance measures for forecast accuracy, plan attainment, supply coverage, inventory exposure, decision quality, capital efficiency, and revenue alignment. Lead root-cause analysis and continuous improvement across planning processes, data, and systems.
Convert large, incomplete, and sometimes conflicting data sets into concise executive narratives, business reviews, decision memos, dashboards, and presentations that clearly communicate assumptions, trade-offs, risks, and required decisions.
Anticipate organization-wide risks and execution bottlenecks, mobilize the appropriate subject-matter experts, and drive resolution across organizational boundaries.
Act as a force multiplier by developing repeatable planning standards, mentoring partner teams, raising the operating standard, and influencing outcomes without relying on direct authority.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in engineering, computer science, supply chain, operations, business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of relevant experience in technical program management, capacity or demand planning, supply chain operations, cloud infrastructure, or related disciplines.
Proven experience leading large-scale, cross-functional programs and delivering measurable business impact in complex, matrixed organizations.
Strong business acumen and demonstrated expertise in forecasting, scenario modeling, product lifecycle planning, supply-demand balancing, operational planning, and risk management.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, balance competing priorities, and translate strategic demand into executable, supply- and site-constrained plans.
Experience supporting senior and executive leadership through strategic planning, business reviews, resource prioritization, and operational decision-making.
Exceptional written, verbal, and executive presentation skills, with the ability to influence technical and business leaders at all levels.
Advanced analytical capabilities and experience converting technical, operational, financial, and customer inputs into actionable recommendations.

Experience with hyperscale cloud, AI/GPU infrastructure, data center capacity, or server, storage, and networking hardware.
Experience leading NPI-to-scale transitions, S&OP or integrated business planning processes, and long-lead supplier or capital decisions.
Experience with financial and business-performance modeling, planning automation, business intelligence, or decision-support systems.
Graduate degree, including an MBA, or relevant program management, supply chain, finance, or operations certification.

Balfour Beatty Construction, LLC (Company), a member of the Balfour Beatty plc group of companies, is searching for a CMMC Program Manager to support its compliance with cyber and physical security requirements for Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) associated with the Company’s Federal construction contracts, as well as equivalent requirements in private contracts. Candidates must have a strong working knowledge of FAR and DFARS requirements for the handling of FCI and CUI, excellent analytical, project management, communication, and organizational skills.

The selected candidate will ideally work out of our Falls Church, VA, office, but candidates based in Dallas, TX, will be considered as well. This is a hybrid position that requires working in the office three days per week and working from home two days per week.

The CMMC Program Manager is responsible for managing, maintaining, and continuously improving the organization's Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) compliance program for the secure enclave supporting Department of Defense (DoD) and other Federal agency CUI, as well as the Company’s policies and procedures for handling FCI. The CMMC Program Manager will serve as the primary liaison between compliance & ethics, IT, legal, and operations as it relates to governance, reporting, monitoring, assessment and organizational adoption of security requirements necessary to maintain ongoing compliance with NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-137, FAR and DFARS requirements, and CMMC Level 1 and Level 2.

Essential Functions

Serve as the organization's primary internal authority for CMMC compliance within the secure enclave, providing guidance to IT, IT Security, Operations, Human Resources, Legal, Procurement, Communications and executive leadership regarding FCI, CUI and equivalent compliance obligations and governance requirements.
Own the organization's CMMC compliance program for the secure enclave, ensuring governance activities remain aligned with organizational objectives, contractual obligations, regulatory requirements, and evolving cybersecurity risks.
Develop, maintain, and periodically review the Continuous Monitoring Plan (CMP) and support ISCM procedures.
Develop, review, maintain, and coordinate approval of CMMC-related policies, standards, procedures, and supporting documentation.
Define and manage ISCM strategy, risk tolerance, and reporting cadence in coordination with the CIO, CISO, CLO, and US Compliance Team.
Lead initial implementation, as well as ongoing assessment of security control effectiveness, including vulnerability identification and reporting, configuration compliance, access reviews, and incident monitoring.
Lead annual CMMC self-assessments, risk assessments, internal audits, certification readiness activities, and coordination with Certified Third-Party Assessment Organizations (C3PAOs) for external CMMC assessments, as applicable.
Present compliance status, risk posture, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and governance committees.
Develop and maintain evidence repositories supporting ongoing internal assessments, external certification activities, and audit readiness.
Ensure compliance documentation—including the System Security Plan (SSP), POA&Ms, policies, procedures, system inventories, data flow diagrams, asset inventories, evidence repositories, and assessment records—remains complete, accurate, and current.
Track, report, coordinate, and validate remediation of deviations, exceptions, and findings discovered during monitoring or risk assessments.
Prepare metrics dashboards and executive reports summarizing enclave risk posture and compliance trends.
Coordinate compliance activities involving third-party service providers supporting the enclave, including review of agreements, security documentation, and shared responsibility requirements.
Review proposed changes to enclave architecture, systems, applications, and operational processes to evaluate potential impacts to CMMC compliance and update compliance documentation as necessary.
Coordinate with IT Operations and IT Security teams to ensure configuration baselines, asset inventories, and system changes remain aligned with approved security configurations and compliance requirements.
Coordinate or participate in periodic incident response tabletop exercises involving IT, Legal, Human Resources, Executive Leadership, and applicable business stakeholders.
Collect evidence management, control documentation, and audit preparation.
Coordinate post-incident reviews, track corrective actions, and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into security controls, policies, procedures, training, and continuous monitoring activities to improve the organization's overall CMMC compliance posture.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders:
Business Stakeholders: program managers, project managers, and functional owners using enclave resources. Assist with onboarding, offboarding and transfers as needed.
Internal and secure enclave MSSP and IT Security Teams: administrators, network engineers, and analysts managing enclave systems and monitoring tools.
Policy and Procedure Enforcement: detect and document deviations or non-compliance, collaborate with HR and/or Legal to resolve violations, and ensure corrective or disciplinary actions are applied and recorded in accordance with organizational policy and audit requirements.
CMMC Training Program Management: review, develop, and adjust security awareness or role-based training content to ensure alignment with current government, DOD, and CMMC requirements and to address evolving cyber security and enclave operational risks.
Executive Leadership: provide compliance reporting, risk briefings, POA&M status, and recommendations for risk acceptance decisions.
Familiarity with export control requirements such as International Traffic in Arms Regulations and Export Administration Regulations.
Continuously review and improve ISCM processes, automation, and reporting frequency to align with organizational risk tolerance.
Facilitate risk assessments and coordinate risk acceptance activities with executive leadership where appropriate.
Supervise and direct security measures necessary for implementing the applicable requirements of the NISPOM and related USG security requirements to ensure the protection of classified information.
Establish and execute an insider threat program to gather, integrate, and report relevant and available information indicative of potential or actual insider threat.
Support broader Ethics & Compliance initiatives, including performing other ethics, compliance, and special projects as assigned by the Vice President, Ethics & Compliance and as workload and business needs permit.

Minimum Qualifications

This position requires access to export-controlled information. To comply with U.S. government regulations and contract obligations applicable so such information, all applicants must be U.S. persons under the U.S. export control regulations.
Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management, Compliance and Regulation, Information Security, Information Systems, or a related field. Equivalent experience working within a Department of Defense agency will also be considered.
7+ years in cybersecurity, governance, risk management, compliance, or information security, including at least 3 years supporting NIST SP 800-171 related programs.
Hands-on experience with NIST SP 800-137 implementation or continuous monitoring frameworks.
Familiarity with NIST SP 800-171, CMMC Level 1 and 2, and FAR and DFARS.
Demonstrated experience developing or managing System Security Plans (SSP) and POA&Ms.
Strong analytical, documentation, and executive-reporting skills.
Ability to coordinate cross-functional teams and enforce accountability.
Complete FSO training within 6 months of hire if not already completed.
Complete ITPSO training.

Preferred Qualifications / Certifications

Experience supporting Department of Defense, Federal Government, or other regulated markets with significant information security requirements.
CMMC: Certified CMMC Professional (CCP) or Certified CMMC Assessor (CCA) or CMMC Registered Practitioner Advanced (RPA)
Cyber security: Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC), Security+ or CySA+
Experience operating in secure enclave or DoD contractor environments.

Performance Indicators

Timeliness and completeness of annual ISCM assessments
Percentage of controls with continuous monitoring coverage
Number of open POA&M items vs. remediation rate
Accuracy and quality of compliance metrics / dashboards
Policy and Procedure enforcement
Successful CMMC C3PAO recertification every 3 years

Pay Rate: $125,000-195,000/year

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, shift, travel requirements, any collective bargaining agreements, and business or organizational needs. No amount of pay is considered to be wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable. The amount and availability of any bonus, incentive, or any other form of compensation that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company's sole discretion, consistent with the law and any applicable plan documents.

Balfour Beatty is an equal opportunity employer that recognizes the value of a diverse workforce. All qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other criteria protected by federal, state or local law.

Ability to solve complex decisions independently

Bachelor's Degree

new_jobs.description:
At Credence, we support our clients' mission-critical needs, powered by technology. We provide cutting-edge solutions, including AI/ML, enterprise modernization, and advanced intelligence capabilities, to the largest defense and health federal organizations. Through partnership and trust, we increase mission success for war-fighters and secure our nation for a better future.
We are privately held, are repeatedly recognized as a top place to work, and have been on the Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies list for the last 12 years. We practice servant leadership and believe that by focusing on the success of our clients, team members, and partners, we all achieve greater success.
Credence has an immediate opening for a Program Manager- PEO Execution Group at the Senior level supporting AFLCMC/WAX at Wright Patterson AFB, OH.
The Plans and Programs Division supports the modernization and sustainment of Fighter and Advanced Aircraft (F&AA) capabilities for the U.S. Air Force and coalition partners. The division manages capability planning, technology integration, program oversight, and cross-functional processes—including airworthiness, configuration management, system safety, and cybersecurity—from concept through fielding. It also develops future capability roadmaps in collaboration with Air Force Major Commands (MAJCOMs) and other key stakeholders.

The Program Manager- PEO Execution Group shall assist in independently applying/demonstrating proficiency in various project/program initiatives.  The Contractor shall assist in investigating, analyzing, planning, designing, developing, implementing, or evaluating solutions for project/program efforts.  The Contractor shall assist in providing expert-level issue resolution and recommendation support to achieve desired program outcomes and have specialized expertise to include the following functional areas: program management, logistics, maintenance, supply, financial management, test, security management, information management, and contracting
Assist in building and maintaining business relationships between the program office, supporting Government offices, other contractors, USAF AFMC, AFLCMC, AFRL, Air Combat Command (ACC), AFGSC, and higher headquarters' mid-to upper-level staff, to support the F/B Capability Plans and Programs for the various platforms
Participate in and represent the interests of the F/B portfolio of programs in the Service Core Function process.  The Contractor shall assist in building business relationships and perform activities necessary to influence science and technology investment decisions favorable to the F/B portfolio of programs.  The Contractor shall assist in performing other related duties associated with F/B capability planning
Possess USAF MAJCOM expertise, ideally at the HQ USAF, HQ ACC, or HQ AFGSC level, as a background for understanding broad user war fighter requirements.  The Contractor shall assist with the analysis of war fighter requirements with ACC and AFGSC and serve as key advisor to Capability Planning leadership on mission critical capability needs
Assist in preparing and reviewing pertinent data, coordinating with applicable managers, and finalizing related documentation/information for verbal and visual presentation of the plan status at meetings as required.  These meetings shall include, but are not limited to, IPT meetings, Program Management Reviews (PMRs), TIMs, working groups, and conferences in support of the F/B portfolio
Support analytic identification of needs and development of requirements for potential materiel solutions.  The Contractor shall assist with the initiation of high confidence acquisition programs via early systems engineering, early test and evaluation strategy development, technology and manufacturing maturity, assessments of life-cycle analyses, lifecycle cost estimates, and early acquisition intelligence engagement
Assist in identifying and solving problems and aid in the influence of science and technology investment decisions.  The Contractor shall assist in developing and executing a collaborative process bridging warfighter-identified capability needs to plan for acquisition of materiel solutions.  The Contractor shall support the trade-space evaluation of emerging capability needs, including system-of-systems assessments.  The Contractor shall assist in identifying and assessing technology maturity and risk drivers and incorporate comprehensive life-cycle planning to include pre-concept through disposal in support of future program technical needs
Assist in applying expertise of the acquisition process and all areas relating to acquisition policy matters, including acquisition streamlining, integrated weapon systems management, manning, best practices and lessons learned, to assigned projects
Support and conduct studies and analysis of tradeoffs for incorporation of potential capabilities in future platform capabilities
Act as the F/B Directorate Unit Control Center Chief for emergency response, exercises, and other surge activities.  The Contractor shall assist in ensuring that PEG and directorate leadership is kept apprised of workload assignments, resolutions and other time sensitive communications/events.  The Contractor shall assist in receiving, preparing, submitting and maintaining official records of documentation and communications.  These activities may be performed as part of an exercise for training purposes or in the event of a real world contingency
Assist in developing and maintaining the F/B Directorate Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) and shall assist in leading the F/B Directorate participation in the AFLCMC COOP and execution
Assist in managing the F/B Directorate SIP.  The Contractor shall assist in identifying and tracking deficiencies during the annual SIP cycle and keep leadership informed as items are closed-out and in preparation for the SIP out-brief meeting.  The Contractor shall assist in utilizing the Management Internal Control Toolset (MICT) and assist in identifying new and/or recently updated SIP checklists for division use as required.  The Contractor shall assist divisions with checklist completion, deficiency tracking, training, and other SIP-related issues.  The Contractor shall hold meetings as required with unit SIP monitors and conduct F/B Directorate SIP training
Support the PEG and DAG processes for the entire F/B Directorate at all locations including but not limited to: MARs, DAES, SARs and and TMTs.
Apply knowledge and experience in acquisition program management policies and procedures to USAF systems, subsystems, and equipment procurement activities, post award project/program management tasks, and acquisition programs throughout their life cycles
Apply a full range of acquisition program management policies/procedures to perform a wide range of acquisition management activities in support of the existing and future F/B Directorate aircraft programs and platforms.
Have an understanding of current DoD and USAF acquisition regulations, guidelines and processes
Support the review of proposals as assigned by the customer.  The Contractor shall assist in the coordination of documentation between functional resources to include: financial management, program management, contracting, CM, engineering, and logistics management.  The Contractor shall assist in consolidating functional inputs into common documents.  The Contractor shall assist in planning for the accomplishment of various program milestones
Provide assistance in risk management, project management, process improvement support, and logistics support.  The Contractor shall participate in process improvement activities as members of, or advisors to, Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) and Product/Process Improvement Working Groups (PIWGs). 
Assist in the collection of programmatic inputs from acquisition programs throughout their life cycles to include: research, develop, produce, test, acquire, field, sustain and modernize existing and advanced war-winning capabilities, on-time and on-cost of the F/B Directorate portfolio for the US
Assist in performing a non-voting, advisory role for program source selections on all acquisition related requirements, as required.  The Contractor shall assist in determining program progress and effectively communicating recommendations orally and in writing to higher organizational management.  The Contractor shall apply program knowledge for developing and coordinating responses to taskers in response to internal and external program inquiries.
Knowledge of development and test activities required to support warfighter Urgent Operational Needs (UON) and Joint Urgent Operational Needs (JUON).  The Contractor shall assist in supporting UON execution teams by providing special knowledge to assist in recommending accelerated test concepts, minimum levels of integration required to satisfy operational need, and trade-offs among risk, schedule, performance, and cost
Assist in producing or reviewing products for program offices use that include business case analyses, trade-off studies, estimates for program office acquisition and logistics requirements, written requirements documents for planned acquisitions, and acquisition strategies and plans
Assist in supporting the program office during Materiel Solution Analysis (MSA), Technology Maturation and Risk Reduction (TMRR), Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD), Production and Deployment, and Operations and Support (O&S) phases, to include all milestone activities.  When requested, the Contractor shall assist in supporting the program office in the specific areas as follows
Assist in performing MSAs leading up to design reviews.  The Contractor shall assist in producing or supporting the development of draft documentation and presentation materials as requested or necessitated by programmatic limits based on cost, schedule and performance
Providing support for strategic scheduling and planning documentation such as the Integrated Master Plan (IMP) and the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) and develop and coordinate a reporting framework for event-based activities during the work efforts. 
Assist in developing, analyzing, and maintaining a master integrated program schedule from concept exploration to fielding a system.  The Contractor shall assist in employing networking software tools and capabilities to support lower tier schedule networking, network statusing, generation of network graphics, assignment of realistic durations and relationships to network elements.  The Contractor shall assist in evaluating weapon system contractor-proposed schedules against Government schedules, assessing Government program office schedules against schedule databases and conducting probabilistic and deterministic risk assessments on both Contractor and Government schedules by performing a Schedule Risk Assessment (SRA) using Monte Carlo simulation-based software.  The Contractor shall assist in utilizing various types of scheduling software and integrate weapon system contractor and Government schedule data with the F/B Directorate's schedule databases
Assist in developing program management strategies to include recommending, initiating, reviewing, developing and implementing activities to accomplish Business Case Analysis (BCA), Cost of Ownership analysis (COO), aging aircraft analysis, process documentation, PWSs, Statement of Work (SOWs), Data Item Descriptions (DIDs), test plans, acquisition plans, Life Cycle Management Plans (LCMPs), Life Cycle Sustainment Plans (LCSPs) Engine Life Management Plans (ELMPs), Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans (QASPs), Acquisition Strategy Panels (ASPs), IMPs, IMSs, Aircraft Information Programs (AIPs), and Aircraft Information Management Plans (AIMPs)
Support the development of contract strategies, Work Breakdown Structures (WBSs) and the completion of program risk assessments to document issues impinging on mileston

Job Overview

Job Title:
Project Manager

Location:
Tampa, FL

Job Responsibilities

Trace Systems is seeking a Project Manager to support a dynamic, multi-disciplined team providing geographically dispersed services to Department of War (DoW) customers. This role is ideal for someone ready to grow into project management while applying strong organizational, communication, and coordination skills. The Project Manager will be responsible for managing project personnel, coordinating day-to-day team activities, and ensuring performance aligns with contractual requirements, customer expectations, and Trace Systems standards.

The ideal candidate will have experience or demonstrated capability in the following areas:

Core Responsibilities

24/7 Prime Contractor Liaison - Serve as the constant point of contact for the prime contractor, ensuring immediate response and support for mission-critical needs.
Leadership & Operational Oversight - Lead the contractor team by setting priorities, driving performance, and aligning efforts with Trace Systems' cost, schedule, and quality expectations. Maintain continuity of operations during staff absences.
Contract & Personnel Management - Oversee all aspects of personnel and project execution to meet contractual, program, and government requirements. Ensure deliverables are completed on time and to standard.
Performance Management - Assess task execution and individual contributions, provide actionable feedback, implement improvements, and uphold a culture of accountability and excellence.
Deployment Coordination - Manage personnel through all deployment phases, leveraging internal service centers for effective planning and execution of both short- and long-term assignments.
Additional Duties - Support evolving program and mission requirements through execution of ad hoc tasks as needed, to include (not exclusive) unrelated business development requirements to be performed off government site and outside of contract duty hours.

The Procurement And Technical Support For TVET Career Platform Project In Sri Lanka Will Reduce Unemployment Of Youth, By Creating a Career Platform, With Quality Career Development And Guidance Services. There Are Three Key Outputs That The Project Needs To Deliver

Output 1 : TVET Career Platform is developed and operational

Output 2 : Service Providers’ capacities in TVET Career Platform are strengthened

Output 3 : TVET Career Platform is widely disseminated and utilised among employers and prospect employees.

Job Description

We are seeking a highly motivated Business Program Manager
to lead cross-functional business initiatives that support key organizational priorities. This role requires an experienced program manager who thrives in fast-paced environments, quickly adapts to changing business needs, and consistently delivers high-quality results against aggressive timelines.

The ideal candidate is an organized, proactive professional with strong program management, stakeholder engagement, and analytical skills. They are comfortable navigating ambiguity, driving execution across multiple teams, and leveraging AI and automation to improve operational efficiency and business processes.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Lead cross-functional business programs from planning through execution, ensuring successful delivery of initiatives on time and within scope.
Develop detailed program plans, timelines, milestones, and success metrics while effectively managing competing priorities.
Partner with business, operations, finance, and technical teams to coordinate activities, resolve dependencies, and drive program execution.
Monitor program progress, identify risks and issue, and proactively develop mitigation plans to keep initiatives on track.
Prepare clear and concise program updates, executive presentations, and status reports for stakeholders and leadership.
Analyze program data and performance metrics to identify trends, recommend improvements, and support data-driven decision-making.
Build strong working relationships across cross-functional teams to ensure alignment and successful delivery of business objectives.
Leverage AI tools and automation technologies to streamline workflows, improve productivity, and reduce manual effort.
Drive continuous process improvement by identifying opportunities to simplify and standardize business operations.
Demonstrate ownership, accountability, and adaptability while managing multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, Management, Engineering, or a related field.
7+ years of professional experience, including 5+ years of experience managing cross-functional business or technical programs.
Experience delivering complex programs with multiple stakeholders while meeting challenging timelines.
Experience working with Supply Chain, Operations, or related business functions.
Strong experience partnering with Finance teams on planning, budgeting, forecasting, or business operations.

Join us as an Industrial Project Manager
and lead initiatives that transform how we operate. In this role, you will drive plant-level planning transformation, implement Engineer-to-Order (ETO) standard processes, and lead cross-functional projects that improve operational performance, productivity, quality, and sustainability. You will partner with plant leadership and key stakeholders to execute strategic initiatives, champion continuous improvement, and deliver measurable business results.

What will you do?

Lead the implementation and adoption of ETO standard planning processes across the plant's end-to-end planning activities.
Manage industrial transformation and continuous improvement projects, ensuring delivery on scope, schedule, budget, and business objectives.
Coordinate cross-functional teams and align stakeholders around shared project goals that support plant and organizational priorities.
Coach and support planning teams on standard methodologies, best practices, and process excellence.
Drive the Schneider Performance System (SPS) within the planning function by establishing improvement objectives, monitoring progress, and ensuring sustainable results.
Establish planning standards, governance processes, and key performance metrics to improve consistency and operational effectiveness.
Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including service levels, lead times, forecast accuracy, project milestones, and operational performance.
Identify, assess, and mitigate project and operational risks to maintain momentum and ensure successful outcomes.
Develop and execute transformation roadmaps focused on critical improvements and measurable business impact.
Partner with Planning Managers, Plant Leadership, and Transformation Leaders to drive change management initiatives and address performance gaps.
Leverage digital tools and technologies to improve planning visibility, project execution, collaboration, and decision-making.
Foster a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, innovation, and best-practice sharing across the organization.

What skills and capabilities will make you successful?

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Management, Supply Chain, Operations Management, or a related field is required.
5+ years of leadership experience in Operations, Supply Chain Planning, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or Project Management.

Strong project management skills, including project planning, execution, resource management, budgeting, and risk mitigation.
Experience leading change management efforts and driving successful adoption of new processes and technologies.
Ability to define project objectives and translate business goals into actionable plans.
Strong influencing skills with the ability to drive alignment across cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
Customer and stakeholder-focused mindset with a commitment to delivering business results.
Digital literacy and experience leveraging technology and data to improve operational and project performance.
Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality, compliance, and operational standards.

new_jobs.title: Business Operations Manager, Business Marketing
new_jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Business Marketing team contributes to our broader mission of ensuring responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence by developing and executing strategies that drive awareness, engagement, and usage for OpenAI’s products and platform amongst core business audiences.

The Strategy & Operations function supports Business Marketing with operating models and cadences; strategic planning; portfolio, resource, and investment management; measurement and organizational learning that empower our teams to move at pace with clarity and confidence.

This is a hybrid role, based in San Francisco Bay Area (preferred) or New York City three days a week.

About The Role

Business Marketing moves quickly, and this role sits close to the work. We’re looking for an analytical, highly collaborative Business Operations Manager who can turn a complex marketing budget into better day-to-day decisions. You will partner with marketing leaders, Strategic Finance, Procurement, Data Science, agencies, and regional teams to plan and pace spend, manage commitments, answer urgent questions, and translate investment data into clear actions. This role is not for someone who prefers back-office operations. You will be embedded in the business, understand what teams are trying to achieve, and help them move faster with confidence.

You will run the operating rhythm for budget administration across a global, highly matrixed team: maintaining a trusted view of allocations, POs, contracts, actuals, forecasts, and risks; reconciling inputs across different marketing functions, regions, and shared services; and surfacing tradeoffs for leadership and Strategic Finance. You will also partner with Data Science to better connect spend to outcomes, lead useful ad hoc analysis, and build AI-enabled tools and workflows that take the friction out of budget management and make the information more timely, intuitive, and genuinely useful.

In This Role, You Will

Own day-to-day budget administration across allocations, forecasts, commitments, purchase requests, purchase orders, invoices, accruals, actuals, and reconciliation.
Partner with Business Marketing leadership and Strategic Finance to operationalize allocation decisions, maintain forecasts, prepare scenarios, and surface tradeoffs.
Work side-by-side with marketing leaders across campaigns, events, agencies, contractors, regions, and shared services to plan, pace, track, and manage spend.
Manage the purchasing and contract lifecycle with Procurement, Finance, Legal, agencies, contractors, and vendors, including POs, SOWs, renewals, rate cards, and commitments.
Maintain a trusted global view of spend; reconcile conflicting inputs, identify variances, duplicate costs, timing differences, and at-risk spend, and escalate material issues early.
Build models, dashboards, and ad hoc analyses that connect investments to business goals and help leaders decide what to fund, reduce, defer, challenge, or escalate.
Partner with Data Science and Analytics to improve how Business Marketing understands ROI, effectiveness, and the relationship between spend and outcomes.

You Might Thrive In This Role, If You

Bring 4+ years of experience in business operations, strategic finance, FP&A, marketing operations, business analytics, consulting, or a related quantitative role in a fast-moving, matrixed organization; B2B business understanding preferred.
Strong hands-on experience with significant, at scale budgets, forecasts, purchase orders, commitments, accruals, invoices, and reconciliation.
Excellent analytical skills and genuine curiosity: you enjoy digging into messy data, answering ad hoc questions, and finding the business story behind the numbers.
Practical understanding of purchasing, contracts, agencies, vendors, and the operational details that keep spend moving responsibly.
Ability to communicate clearly, build trust with marketers and finance partners, and create alignment across different marketing functions, regions, and shared services without formal authority.
An AI-native builder mindset: you see a repetitive spreadsheet, approval, reconciliation, or reporting task and start thinking about how to make it simpler, faster, and more useful.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link.

OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy

At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies, and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

Role

The Implementation Manager owns the deployment of Peregrine's platform across a portfolio of public safety customers. You will direct AI agents through configuration and integration, keep concurrent projects moving, and hold every deployment accountable from kickoff through go-live. In this highly focused role, you will work against a clear metric: timely, successful launches—and we're looking for someone who takes real pride in that.

As An Implementation Manager, You Will

Own the end-to-end deployment lifecycle for a portfolio of customers — from initial kickoff through network connectivity, data source integration, QA, permissions configuration, training, and go-live
Direct AI agents to execute integrations, configure ontologies and data models, and set up customer-specific front-end configurations — translating customer requirements into high-quality agent inputs and rigorously validating outputs
Drive and unblock network access and data source connectivity, including internal coordination with Peregrine's infrastructure and engineering teams and direct engagement with customer IT stakeholders
Facilitate virtual kickoffs and working sessions to align customer stakeholders, establish a project cadence, and map the human terrain of each agency
Run lean, self-service-oriented QA and training sessions that upskill customer POCs to validate their own data and engage Peregrine directly — rather than creating dependency on Peregrine staff
Manage permissions configuration end-to-end: gathering requirements via structured intake, directing agents to translate them into Peregrine, and testing outputs by impersonating roles
Maintain rigorous task management across a concurrent portfolio of deployments, surfacing blockers and escalating with urgency
Identify patterns across your book of business to refine agent prompts, improve deployment playbooks, and raise quality across every future deployment

What Success Looks Like

Deployments you manage achieve significant improvements in speed-to-value, go-live times, and sustained user adoption across the organization
Customer POCs leave your QA and training sessions capable of engaging Peregrine's self-service tools independently, without calling you first
Blockers — whether in networking, credential validation, or customer IT — get surfaced and resolved within hours, not days
Your agent prompts and deployment playbooks improve measurably over time, reducing variance in go-live quality across your portfolio

About You

You are a relentless project manager. You track every open item across your portfolio and hold every stakeholder — internal and external — accountable with precision and care
You are fluent in the language of data systems without necessarily being a data engineer. You know what a credential string is, can tell when a data source isn't connecting, and can work with an engineering team to diagnose and unblock it
You are skilled at navigating complex organizations where individuals may require some AI-upskilling. When there are roadblocks in customer deployments, you stay calm and find the path forward anyway
You are a clear, direct communicator — in writing and in live sessions — and you default to structured, asynchronous information-gathering over unnecessary meetings
You are genuinely curious about AI tooling. You'll be one of the first people at Peregrine to manage a portfolio of deployments primarily through agents, and you'll have strong opinions about how to make that better over time
You are a thoughtful trainer. You know the difference between a customer who is truly self-sufficient and one who just thinks they are — and you close that gap before you sign off

What we look for

3–6 years of experience in enterprise software implementation, technical project management, or customer-facing deployment roles
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent implementation projects against tight timelines
Comfort with technical concepts — data connectivity, credential management, permissions structures, data model configuration — without necessarily writing code
Exceptional written communication and documentation skills; you send clear, structured updates and leave no ambiguity about next steps
Experience working with customers that have limited IT resources or low technical sophistication — public sector or government experience a strong plus
High agency, low ego. You figure things out and you keep moving

The Opportunity

Join Adobe as a Program Manager, Transformation, where you will play a pivotal role in driving impactful technology initiatives. This high-utility, flexible role is a great fit for someone who is comfortable with ambiguity and can swiftly adapt to new domains. You will work within a small team of program leaders, contributing to enterprise transformation programs and establishing guidelines that ensure future transformations are repeatable and reliable. Your expertise will be crucial in determining where your skills can yield the greatest benefit to Adobe.

The scope here is broad. You will lead transformation programs end-to-end and, as the portfolio demands, take on specialized responsibilities that span data migration and end-to-end business architecture. You should be equally comfortable ramping on an unfamiliar program and building the reusable standards that make the next program start further ahead.

What You'll Do

Take ownership of transformation programs or workstreams as they arise, ramping quickly and establishing structure, cadence, and momentum.
Partner with FTMO leadership, business users, and technical teams to understand the vision, objectives, and scope of each initiative.
Curate program timelines, roadmaps, and governance — meeting cadence, RAID logs, status reporting, and key artifacts (steering, operating committee, wiki/SharePoint).
Coordinate execution across multi-disciplinary teams; proactively manage risks, issues, dependencies, and changes.
Drive decisions and clear, accurate communication across technical and business audiences.
Flex across the delivery lifecycle — planning, execution, cutover, Hypercare, and decommissioning — depending on where the program needs support.
Measure adoption and impact post-release (30/60/90-day check-ins) and feed insights back into the portfolio.
Adopt and reinforce FTMO best-practice playbooks (migration, cutover, testing, Hypercare, environment/process architecture) on every program, and contribute improvements back to the standard.
On programs that require it, own data migration end-to-end (strategy, plan, ETL cycles, reconciliation, and sign-off) as the single point of accountability, and build the reusable enterprise migration standard that future programs adopt.
When assigned, orchestrate end-to-end business architecture — sequencing environment readiness across the program lifecycle and designing the business process hand-offs across workstreams so the assembled program delivers a coherent end-to-end experience.

new_jobs.title: Business Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Bluebono is building connective infrastructure for the next generation of real estate credit, with a focus on underserved and overlooked market opportunities. Through specialized lending solutions, innovative sourcing, and flexible capital structures, Bluebono connects real estate developers, investors, originators, and institutional capital.
Our platform integrates underwriting, analytics, risk evaluation, servicing, and portfolio management to deliver faster execution, better visibility, and more scalable outcomes across the lending lifecycle.

Role Description

Bluebono is seeking a Business Data Analyst to help build the data foundation and analytical models supporting our lending platform. This role will organize and connect data across the loan lifecycle, develop financial and predictive models, and translate complex information into practical recommendations for management, underwriting, operations, and capital markets.
The ideal candidate combines technical ability with business judgment and is interested in applying data science and machine learning to real-world credit, pricing, risk, and portfolio decisions.

Key ResponsibilitiesData Architecture and Modeling

Design scalable data models covering the loan lifecycle, from initial inquiry and pricing through underwriting, funding, servicing, payoff, or loan sale.
Consolidate data from loan origination, servicing, accounting, CRM, property, pricing, and capital-markets systems.
Build reliable datasets and automated data pipelines for analysis, financial modeling, and machine-learning applications.
Establish consistent data definitions, business rules, validation controls, and documentation across systems.
Identify and resolve missing, duplicated, or inconsistent data in partnership with business teams.

Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics

Develop, test, and refine models supporting lending and operational decisions.
Perform feature engineering using borrower, property, loan, transaction, market, and historical performance data.
Explore applications such as lead conversion, closing probability, pricing, credit risk, loan duration, delinquency, property valuation, fraud detection, investor matching, and liquidity forecasting.
Train, validate, document, and monitor models for accuracy, stability, explainability, bias, and data drift.
Translate model results into clear recommendations while maintaining appropriate human review for material credit and pricing decisions.

Lending and Portfolio Analysis

Analyze loan production, underwriting outcomes, funding activity, servicing performance, payoffs, and loan sales.
Evaluate key metrics including conversion, processing time, LTV, LTC, LTARV, pricing, revenue, funding cost, margin, loan duration, delinquency, concentration, and realized profitability.
Compare projected economics and model predictions with actual results.
Identify trends affecting loan performance, credit quality, operational efficiency, and capital deployment.
Support scenario analysis and stress testing across changes in interest rates, property values, liquidity, and market conditions.

Financial and Capital Markets Modeling

Build loan-level and portfolio-level profitability and cash-flow models.
Analyze funding costs, interest and fee income, servicing revenue, sale proceeds, and transaction expenses.
Model payoff timing, portfolio turnover, liquidity needs, and capital utilization.
Compare performance across products, origination channels, funding sources, and institutional loan purchasers.
Support whole-loan sales, investor reporting, and portfolio-management decisions with accurate loan-level analysis.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Business Analytics, Finance, Economics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field.
At least two years of experience in data analysis, data modeling, machine learning, financial modeling, or a related role.
Strong proficiency in Python, SQL, and Excel.
Experience with data-analysis and machine-learning tools such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
Understanding of regression, classification, clustering, time-series analysis, feature engineering, and model validation.
Ability to work with data from multiple systems and identify gaps, inconsistencies, and unreliable assumptions.
Ability to explain technical findings clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Strong attention to detail, ownership, organization, and business judgment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in mortgage lending, private credit, real estate finance, banking, fintech, or asset management.
Familiarity with bridge, fix-and-flip, construction, or DSCR lending.
Experience building credit-risk, pricing, fraud-detection, property-valuation, prepayment, or cash-flow models.
Experience with APIs, cloud databases, data warehouses, and automated data pipelines.
Understanding of loan origination, servicing, warehouse financing, or whole-loan sales.
Familiarity with model governance, explainability, performance monitoring, and financial-services compliance.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will help Bluebono establish a reliable data foundation, develop models tied to measurable business needs, and turn operational data into better decisions across pricing, underwriting, risk management, capital efficiency, and portfolio performance.

new_jobs.title: Research Analyst - Evidence Aggregation and Data Science at Northwestern University
new_jobs.description:
Research Analyst – Evidence Aggregation and Data Science

Global Poverty Research Lab, Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University

What does the Lab do?

The Global Poverty Research Lab (GPRL) is a research center based at Northwestern University that accelerates poverty reduction by generating frontier research and creating public goods in the form of data, methods, and syntheses, to enable others to design, test, and turn evidence into action.

Projects At GPRL Cut Across The Following Pillars

Frontier Research: Generate cutting edge research in development economics including themes of mental health, agriculture, social protection, and renewable energy; co-create and maintain long-run panels with local universities, governments, and civil society that enable longer-term insights and support layered RCTs.
Advance Research Methods: Build and test better ways to measure and learn, from questionnaire design and enumerator recruitment to rapid-cycle experiments (A/B, factorial, micro-randomized) that implementers can run using their own administrative data to tune delivery models, incentives, and other protocols.
Aggregate Global Evidence: Building semi-automated pipelines and AI-assisted workflows to compile and structure scattered evidence from RCTs into living knowledge bases and run rigorous meta-analyses; deliver insights via evidence syntheses, interactive dashboards, and publicly accessible data for donors, investors, and practitioners.
Making Aid More Effective: Turn evidence into ready-to-use decision tools, “smart buys” menus, and ROI/cost-effectiveness frameworks for donors, ministries, multilaterals, impact investors, and social enterprises.

Our Team

GPRL is co-directed by Dean Karlan, Christopher Udry, and Nancy Qian, professors at the Kellogg School of Management and the Weinberg School of Arts and Sciences’ Economics department at Northwestern University. Other actively affiliated professors include Andrew Dillon and Lori Beaman. GPRL’s research managers, research analysts, and administrative staff support our investigators’ projects, in the process working closely with colleagues at universities, NGOs, and research institutions around the world.

GPRL also works in close collaboration with research teams at Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) to coordinate field data collection, disseminate evidence, and create shared training and research resources.

Job Summary

GPRL is hiring 2 full-time Research Analyst – Evidence Aggregation and Data Science to support our Evidence Aggregation Initiative, a multi-institution effort to build scalable, AI-assisted infrastructure for compiling and synthesizing evidence from randomized controlled trials in development economics. The initiative spans the full pipeline from study selection and AI-assisted data extraction to microdata harmonization, meta-analysis, and public dissemination — with the goal of making the best available evidence on what works for whom more accessible to researchers, policymakers, and donors worldwide.

This position offers a rare opportunity to work at the intersection of data science, AI, and development economics research. The RA will contribute to a live, rapidly evolving pipeline at a moment when the project is scaling up from a pilot phase to broader operations. They will gain hands-on experience building and maintaining research data infrastructure, working with large language models in applied research contexts, conducting quantitative analysis, and supporting the management of a distributed network of data validators. The role suits candidates with strong technical skills who are equally motivated by the real-world impact of the work.

Core Responsibilities

Supporting the operation and iterative improvement of the AI-assisted data extraction pipeline, including monitoring extraction accuracy, identifying fields where AI performance requires refinement, and contributing to validation workflows
Cleaning, organizing, and quality-checking data extracted from several published RCT papers into DEVIDENCE, GPRL's relational database of study-level metadata and treatment effects, and preparing it for use in cross-study analyses.
Cleaning and organizing study microdata from published RCTs and validating their replication packages to prepare them for harmonization and cross-study analyses.
Supporting the crowdsourcing platform through which a distributed network of external validators review and adjudicate AI-extracted data, including helping to onboard new cohorts of validators, tracking coder performance, and identifying and resolving data quality issues
Conducting quantitative analysis using the harmonized data, including contributing to meta-analyses and evidence reviews, preparing tables and figures, and assisting with revisions to working papers and publications
Supervising undergraduate RAs engaged in data extraction and validation tasks, including providing training, reviewing work, and maintaining coding documentation
Contributing to the development and refinement of training materials, coding guides, and documentation that support both internal staff and the external validator community
Assisting with the design and implementation of data harmonization protocols for select outcome variables across studies, including writing and reviewing code that standardizes variables for cross-study comparability
Supporting project management and dissemination tasks, including tracking project milestones, preparing materials for funder and partner communications, and contributing to grant proposals and reports
Conducting literature reviews in support of meta-analyses, evidence syntheses, and grant proposals
Supporting research staff with Lab-wide management tasks including mentoring new RAs, creating research and training resources, and supporting with recruitment

Minimum Competencies

Strong programming skills in R, combined with a willingness to learn other statistical software. Strong quantitative skills, including coursework in statistics, econometrics, or a related quantitative field
Familiarity with randomized controlled trials
Excellent organizational skills
Fluency and excellent communication skills in English
Ability to seek resources and self-teach new statistical, analytical, and programming techniques
Flexible, self-motivating, able to manage multiple tasks efficiently, and work in teams

Preferred Competencies

Familiarity with relational databases and structured data (e.g., SQL or equivalent experience working with multi-table datasets)
Experience living or working in a developing country
Experience with reproducible research workflows, version control (GitHub), and modern documentation tools (Quarto, R Markdown)
Familiarity with meta-analytic methods or systematic review approaches
Demonstrated ability to build data quality assurance systems and manage collaborative data projects
Experience using advanced data infrastructure such as relational databases, API connections, and cloud computing
Familiarity with Stata and/or Python preferred
Familiarity working with a variety of machine learning models
Familiarity with other statistical, visualization or digital data collection software like ArcGIS/Python/SurveyCTO is a strong plus

The research analyst will work in an open, collaborative environment with other GPRL staff in our common lab space at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois (bordering Chicago). The position offers the opportunity to interact with undergraduates, graduate students, and faculty from Kellogg and the department of economics at Northwestern, as well as research staff at IPA. It is well-suited for candidates interested in pursuing graduate study in economics or other social sciences in the future. It is also a great steppingstone for those wanting to explore non-academic careers in the field of development economics. The research analyst will be a full-time employee of Northwestern University with full benefits (including the ability to take classes at a highly subsidized tuition rate).

We are looking for a minimum commitment of two years for this position.

Non-immigrant visa sponsorship for this role is subject to country-specific restrictions determined by the US Department of State. Since these regulations are regularly revised, we advise applicants to review the current restrictions before applying.

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority is North America's largest transportation network, serving a population of 15.3 million people across a 5,000-square-mile travel area surrounding New York City, Long Island, southeastern New York State, and Connecticut. The MTA network comprises the nation’s largest bus fleet and more subway and commuter rail cars than all other U.S. transit systems combined. MTA strives to provide a safe and reliable commute, excellent customer service, and rewarding opportunities.

Job Summary

The Performance and Strategy Analyst Level I supports the Office of Consolidated Pensions by driving operational excellence, elevating performance measurement, and advancing strategic modernization initiatives across pension operations.

This role builds the analytical foundation for performance management by developing key performance indicators (KPIs) and objectives and key results (OKRs), creating data-driven tools such as Power BI dashboards, and supporting process improvement efforts. This level focuses on strengthening day‑to‑day operational insight, enabling efficient decision-making, and enhancing the member experience through accurate, timely, and measurable service delivery.

Across both levels, the Performance and Strategy Analyst exists to provide the analytical, performance‑management, and strategic support required for a modern, high-performing pension function. Examples of duties include designing new analytical frameworks—such as a suite of Power BI dashboards covering monthly pension inceptions, benefit calculations, retroactive payments, death benefits, Tier 6 member data, and disability retirement processing—and ensuring these tools draw directly from PeopleSoft where possible. The role also contributes to defining and tracking KPIs and/or OKRs to benchmark and continually improve pension operations.

Responsibilities

Develops and maintains performance measurement frameworks (Key Performance Indicators and Objectives and Key Results) to monitor operational efficiency and strategic progress, ensuring leadership has actionable insights for decision-making.
Leads the creation and continuous improvement of the Operations Playbook by documenting core pension processes and workflows to standardize practices and support organizational modernization.
Coordinates and tracks strategic technology enhancements, including targeted PeopleSoft improvements such as end-to-end workflow for pension inceptions, to expand automation and improve the member experience.
Designs and produces monthly and quarterly performance dashboards and reports to provide transparency on operational outcomes and progress toward strategic objectives.
Supports organizational decision-making by developing and managing a lightweight, repeatable decision framework that accelerates approvals and ensures decisions are data‑driven and documented for accountability
Conducts process mapping and analysis to identify bottlenecks and recommend improvements that reduce cycle times, enhance accuracy, and strengthen compliance.
Prepares benchmarking readiness materials, including cost‑per‑member and service‑level metrics, to position the organization for participation in CEM global pension benchmarking and other industry best‑practice comparisons.
Facilitates and supports team workshops focused on agile practices, trust‑building, and integration planning to foster a culture of continuous improvement and collaboration.
Performs other duties as assigned

Addresses performance issues with the contractor when possible, as applicable

Required Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Knowledge of data analysis concepts, performance measurement practices, and basic process‑improvement methodologies, with the ability to apply these skills to public pension operations.
Working knowledge of pension plan member data or other public‑sector benefits data, including understanding data structures, data quality considerations, and operational workflows.
Skill in analyzing operational data related to public pension administration, such as benefit processing timelines, member transactions, and service‑delivery metrics.
Proficiency with Power BI, including the ability to build dashboards, create visualizations, and connect to enterprise data sources such as PeopleSoft.

Strong analytical, critical‑thinking, and problem‑solving skills, with the ability to identify inefficiencies and propose solutions.

Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to work across teams, gather requirements, and present findings to leadership.

Curiosity, initiative, and the willingness to develop deeper subject‑matter expertise in pension operations over time.

Required Education And Experience

Minimum 1 year of experience. The role is designed for an early‑career analyst who can apply strong analytical skills immediately while developing deeper expertise in pension operations over time.

The Following Is/are Preferred
