Minimum 1 year practical experience working with pension plan member data or other public‑sector benefits data is preferred, including exposure to data validation, workflow analysis, or service‑delivery metrics.
Minimum 1 year experience analyzing public pension plan operational data—such as member transactions, benefit processing timelines, or workload volumes—and translating those insights into dashboards or structured reports is highly valuable.
Minimum 1 year of proficiency building Power BI dashboards, particularly using PeopleSoft or similar enterprise systems as data sources, is strongly preferred.

Job Description

Oracle Health Government Services is seeking an experienced Lead Federal Project Manager (Intake Lead) to join our mission-driven organization and provide program-wide leadership for the Technical Intake Process supporting the federal portfolio, including the Department of War (DOW), Indian Health Service (IHS), Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and new federal clients.

The ideal candidate will have extensive experience leading cross-functional programs in federal environments and demonstrated success coordinating across project management, engineering, enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, product, hosting, release management, and client delivery organizations. This role serves as a primary point of coordination and escalation across multiple federal clients and governance forums, ensuring technical requests are appropriately evaluated, documented, prioritized, resourced, and advanced from initial intake through feasibility analysis and contract award. The successful candidate will be highly organized, comfortable operating independently with limited oversight, and skilled at driving accountability, removing blockers, communicating with senior stakeholders, and continuously improving program processes.

Establish strong working relationships across federal program leadership, Project Managers, technical teams, Product, Hosting, Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, Release Management, and client-facing organizations.

Experience with Oracle Health technologies, Federal EHR programs, cloud technologies, and/or large-scale healthcare technology implementations strongly preferred.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Must Have Technical/Functional Skills

15+ years in IT delivery with a minimum of 10+ years in a dedicated Project Manager role — must have successfully led at least two large-scale, cross-functional projects to completion across different project types such as system migrations, digital transformations, platform implementations, or new product launches
Strong command of both Agile and Waterfall delivery methodologies — ability to apply the right framework to the right context, and to manage hybrid projects where different workstreams operate under different delivery models simultaneously
Expertise in project governance — ability to set up and run a full governance structure from scratch: RAID log, steering committee, change control board, escalation matrix, and status reporting cadence tailored to the project's complexity and stakeholder expectations
Proficiency in project planning and tracking tools — Jira, MS Project, Confluence, Smartsheet, or equivalent — and advanced reporting using Excel or Power BI to build executive-level dashboards and project health views
Financial management skills — experience owning a project budget, tracking actuals vs. forecast on a T&M or fixed-price basis, managing scope change requests with impact assessments, and presenting financial status to senior leadership
Proven experience managing large vendor delivery partnerships — defining SOWs, tracking against contractual deliverables, running governance reviews with vendor leadership, and holding delivery teams accountable without creating adversarial dynamics
Ability to manage and coordinate multiple parallel workstreams — architecture, engineering, data, QA, security, infrastructure, and business readiness — ensuring dependencies are mapped, sequenced, and tracked across the full project lifecycle
Experience with organizational change management — identifying business impact of project changes, developing stakeholder communication plans, managing resistance, and ensuring teams and end users are ready before go-live
Strong experience with risk management — identifying project-level risks early, building credible mitigation plans, quantifying risk exposure, and escalating only what genuinely requires SLT intervention with recommended options attached
PMP or PgMP certification is mandatory — not preferred, not in progress; candidate must hold an active, valid certification from PMI at time of joining; demonstrates proven command of project lifecycle, governance, risk, and financial controls across structured delivery frameworks
Must demonstrate mastery of the triple constraint — cost, schedule, and scope — and be able to independently build a detailed financial plan, Gantt chart, integrated project schedule, and milestone tracker from day one; these are non-negotiable delivery tools, not optional outputs
Budget management depth is required — candidate must be able to track weekly actuals, manage committed spend (POs, signed contracts), maintain a rolling forecast, calculate Estimate at Completion (EAC), explain variance, and present a complete financial picture to leadership with root cause and corrective action
Full working knowledge of SOW types and contract models — Fixed Fee SOW (vendor carries risk, scope must be fully defined), Time & Materials SOW (client pays actuals, requires tight burn rate governance), and Cost Plus SOW (actuals + agreed margin); must know when each applies, how to govern it, and how to protect the program from overrun under each model
Leadership bar — this role is expected to raise the standard for everyone around them; the right candidate will push engineers, vendors, and business stakeholders to deliver at a higher level, hold people accountable without micromanaging, and create a culture where the team does not need to be chased for updates
Fully onsite 5 days a week in Parsippany, NJ — this is a non-negotiable requirement; the program requires in-person leadership presence, real-time stakeholder engagement, and direct team visibility; remote or hybrid arrangements will not be considered for this role

Roles & Responsibilities

Own full accountability for project delivery across scope, schedule, budget, quality, and risk — from project initiation through delivery, go-live, and stabilization; the project's success or failure is this role's responsibility
Define the project roadmap and integrated delivery plan at the outset — break the project into logical phases or waves, identify the critical path, map all workstream dependencies, and establish milestones that stakeholders can hold the team to
Establish and operate project governance from day one — steering committee cadence, RAID log, change control board, decision log, and status reporting framework; governance must be operational before delivery teams begin work, not retrofitted after problems appear
Manage vendor and partner delivery organizations — own the SOW and contractual obligations, run regular governance reviews, enforce SLA commitments, escalate vendor performance issues through the right channels, and document all delivery decisions
Drive cross-functional workstream alignment — chair dependency resolution sessions, maintain the integrated dependency log, assign ownership to every cross-team dependency, and track resolution to closure before it becomes a blocker
Own project financial management — track T&M actuals and forecast weekly, manage change requests through formal scope change process with full impact assessment on budget, schedule, and risk, and present financial health to SLT with transparency
Facilitate and own Agile project ceremonies where applicable — PI Planning, System Demos, Inspect and Adapt workshops — ensuring all teams have clear objectives, dependencies mapped, and capacity planned for each increment
Proactively manage the RAID log — identify risks before they become issues, assign owners, review mitigation progress weekly, and escalate items that exceed the project's risk tolerance with clear options and a recommended course of action
Lead change management activities — assess the organizational impact of the project, build a stakeholder communication plan, ensure business readiness activities (training, process change, cutover preparation) are tracked as project deliverables not afterthoughts
Be the single accountable point of contact for project health — provide weekly written status reports and participate in steering committee meetings with an honest, metric-backed view of progress, risks, and decisions needed; never present a rosier picture than reality supports

Be a subject matter expert with contract documents for each assigned project including, but not limited to project scopes of work, bid drawings and specifications, contract, subcontractor scopes of work, and construction schedules.

HII designs, develops, integrates and manages the sensors, systems and other assets necessary to support integrated ISR operations and accelerated decision-making. With data fusion and mission management capabilities for the Department of Defense, the combatant commands and the intelligence community, HII advances the mission around the globe.

Leadership Mindset at HII – Mission Technologies

Role

Leadership at HII is a mindset, not a title. Through our Leadership Capability Framework, we define how every employee grows, leads, and contributes—regardless of role. It sets the standard for how you can develop yourself and what you can expect from leaders across our organization. We look for candidates who want to grow in alignment with these capabilities:

Know & Grow Your People – Commit to learning and supporting team success.
Build Relationships – Communicate openly, collaborate well, and build trust.
Take Ownership – Deliver on commitments and take pride in your work.
Customer First – Focus on the mission and those we serve.
Shape the Future – Bring ideas, curiosity, and continuous improvement.
Act with Urgency – Take initiative and follow through with purpose.

These capabilities guide how all employees contribute to our shared success across Mission Technologies.

Who We Are

HII-Mission Technologies is seeking a Intermediate Screening and Vetting Analyst to support the Office of National Security (ONS) within the Immediate Office of the Secretary at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). ONS manages Department-wide programs and provides oversight, policy direction, standards, and performance assessments in the areas of counterintelligence, intelligence, insider threat, cyber threat intelligence, information security, national personnel security, homeland security, and the safeguarding of classified information.

ONS provides counterintelligence, intelligence, and security support to HHS Operating Divisions, Staff Divisions, and Department leadership. This position will support the Identity Intelligence Division (I2D) and focus on conducting screening, vetting, identity resolution, and risk analysis of foreign nationals, entities, and individuals associated with HHS programs, facilities, grants, contracts, acquisitions, and SBIR/STTR initiatives. The analyst will leverage government, commercial, and open-source information to identify foreign affiliations, indicators of malign foreign influence, counterintelligence concerns, technology transfer risks, and other threats to HHS-funded research, public health programs, and critical supply chains.

What You Will Do

The Screening and Vetting Analyst will conduct all-source intelligence analysis, screening and vetting, identity resolution, network analysis, and risk assessments to identify foreign affiliations, malign foreign influence, counterintelligence concerns, technology transfer risks, and other threats to HHS programs, research, and supply chains. The analyst will produce tailored intelligence products, provide briefings and decision-support to HHS leadership, acquisition officials, program managers, and security personnel, and develop working relationships with key stakeholders to address evolving intelligence and security requirements. The position requires the ability to identify non-obvious relationships between individuals, organizations, foreign governments, talent recruitment programs, and entities of concern; monitor emerging threats; coordinate with Intelligence Community, law enforcement, and interagency partners; participate in working groups and interagency forums; and provide actionable intelligence that supports the protection of HHS-funded research, sensitive information, and national security equities.

What We Are Looking For

5 years of relevant experience with a bachelor's degree in a related field; 3 years of relevant experience with a master's degree in a related field; or a High School Diploma/equivalent and 9 years of relevant experience
Active TS/SCI security clearance
Demonstrated experience conducting screening, vetting, identity resolution, due diligence, risk assessments, or intelligence analysis in support of national security, counterintelligence, homeland security, law enforcement, personnel security, or related missions
Knowledge of foreign influence, non-traditional collection, technology transfer, insider threat, research security, and foreign ownership, control, or influence (FOCI) risks affecting government, academic, research, or commercial environments
Ability to assess and weigh source reliability and credibility, identify assumptions, distinguish facts from judgments, evaluate alternative explanations, and develop defensible analytic conclusions
Experience conducting all-source research and analysis using government, commercial, and open-source data to identify affiliations, relationships, and potential risk indicators associated with individuals, entities, and organizations
Ability to perform identity resolution, network analysis, pattern-of-life analysis, and link analysis to identify non-obvious relationships, foreign affiliations, and potential national security concerns
Demonstrated ability to identify trends, patterns, anomalies, and emerging threats through the synthesis of fragmented information and the identification of critical intelligence gaps
Strong research and collection skills, including identifying relevant data sources, developing collection strategies, and supporting intelligence requirements and key intelligence questions
Experience producing high-quality written intelligence products, risk assessments, executive summaries, and briefing materials tailored to operational and senior leadership audiences
Ability to brief senior leaders on intelligence findings, risk assessments, emerging threats, and screening/vetting outcomes while appropriately conveying confidence levels, uncertainty, and source attribution
Knowledge of Intelligence Community, law enforcement, homeland security, and interagency processes, including the appropriate handling, dissemination, and classification of sensitive information
Excellent technical writing, verbal communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across government, contractor, and interagency partners

Preferred: Bonus Points For...

Ability to manage multiple high-priority screening, vetting, and analytic requirements simultaneously while adapting to evolving mission priorities, emerging threats, and time-sensitive operational demands.
Demonstrated experience engaging with senior government officials, program stakeholders, security professionals, acquisition personnel, and interagency partners on matters involving screening, vetting, risk assessment, counterintelligence, or national security concerns
Familiarity with Security Classification Guides (SCGs), classification management processes, intelligence information handling requirements, and the appropriate protection, dissemination, and safeguarding of classified and sensitive information
Minimum of 3 years of experience conducting intelligence analysis, screening and vetting, personnel security, counterintelligence, identity intelligence, due diligence, risk assessment, or related national security functions, including experience producing written intelligence products, executive-level briefings, and analytic assessments for senior decision-makers
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Adobe Acrobat; experience with analytical, investigative, or link-analysis tools

Physical Requirements

Job performance will normally require only minor lifting and carrying of boxes of records or equipment.

The listed salary range for this role is intended as a good faith estimate based on the role's location, expectations, and responsibilities. When extending an offer, HII's Mission Technologies division takes a variety of factors into consideration which include, but are not limited to, the role's function and a candidate's education or training, work experience, and key skills.

Meet HII’s Mission Technologies Division

Our team of more than 7,000 professionals worldwide delivers all-domain expertise and advanced technologies in service of mission partners across the globe. Mission Technologies is leading the next evolution of national defense – the data evolution - by accelerating a breadth of national security solutions for government and commercial customers. Our capabilities range from C5ISR, AI and Big Data, cyber operations and synthetic training environments to fleet sustainment, environmental remediation and the largest family of unmanned underwater vehicles in every class.
